cue.card: Describe an advertisement that you remember well.
points: and explain why you remember it
model: The advert I remember best was for a mobile network, and I first saw it on TV around Lunar New Year a few years ago.

It told a very simple story. A young man is working in a big city and can’t afford to go home for Tet. His elderly mother doesn’t know how to use a smartphone, so his little niece secretly teaches her, and on New Year’s Eve the mother surprises him with a video call. The whole family appears on the screen, and the slogan at the end is something like “Distance is only a number”.

I remember it for two reasons. First, it was emotional without being misleading — it didn’t claim the network was the fastest or the cheapest, it just showed what the service makes possible. Second, it was very close to my own situation at the time, because I was also working far from home. Honestly, I’ve forgotten most adverts I’ve ever seen, but that one made me phone my parents that evening.

write.prompt: Advertising aimed at children should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + clear position (agree for young children and unhealthy products; total ban too extreme)
Body 1: why children need protection — cannot judge adverts, junk food, pester power
Body 2: why a total ban is unrealistic — educational products, online enforcement, media literacy is better
Conclusion: restate the partial agreement
model: Many people believe that companies should not be allowed to advertise to children at all. While I agree that young children need strong protection, especially from adverts for unhealthy products, I believe a complete ban would be difficult to enforce and is not the most effective solution.

There are good reasons to restrict this kind of advertising. Young children cannot easily distinguish between entertainment and persuasion, so they tend to believe whatever an advert tells them. Much of the marketing aimed at them promotes sugary snacks and expensive toys, which can contribute to poor diets and make children more materialistic. In addition, advertisers deliberately encourage children to pressure their parents into buying products, which creates conflict in families with limited budgets.

However, banning all advertising to children would be unrealistic. Not every advert is harmful: some inform families about books, educational apps or sports clubs. Furthermore, most children now spend their time on international websites and games, where national laws are very hard to apply. In my view, it would be more effective to ban advertising of unhealthy food and to require clear labelling of sponsored content, while schools teach children how adverts try to persuade them.

In conclusion, I partly agree with the statement. Advertising aimed at children should be strictly regulated, and adverts for harmful products should be prohibited, but a total ban is neither practical nor necessary if children are taught to recognise persuasive techniques.

lines.t: Do you prefer travelling in your own country or abroad?

lines.t: At the moment, domestic travel, because it’s cheaper and Vietnam has so much variety, from mountains in the north to islands in the south.
lines.vi: Hiện tại là trong nước, vì rẻ hơn và Việt Nam rất đa dạng, từ núi ở phía bắc đến đảo ở phía nam.

lines.t: What kind of places do you like to visit?
lines.vi: Bạn thích đến những nơi như thế nào?

lines.t: Places off the beaten track. I find famous spots too commercialised, so I’d rather stay in a small village and eat whatever the locals eat.
lines.vi: Những nơi ít người biết. Tôi thấy các điểm nổi tiếng quá thương mại hoá, nên tôi thích ở một ngôi làng nhỏ và ăn những gì người dân ăn.

lines.t: Do you buy souvenirs?
lines.vi: Bạn có mua quà lưu niệm không?

lines.t: Only small, local things, like handmade tea or textiles. I avoid the mass-produced ones you find at every tourist trap.
lines.vi: Chỉ những thứ nhỏ, của địa phương như trà làm tay hay vải dệt. Tôi tránh đồ sản xuất hàng loạt bán ở mọi điểm chặt chém du khách.

sents.t: Venice has about 50,000 residents but receives more than 20 million visitors a year.
sents.vi: Venice có khoảng 50.000 cư dân nhưng đón hơn 20 triệu lượt khách mỗi năm.

sents.t: Rising rents caused by holiday apartments have forced many local families to leave.
sents.vi: Giá thuê tăng do căn hộ cho khách du lịch đã buộc nhiều gia đình địa phương rời đi.

sents.t: In 2024 the city began charging day visitors an entrance fee on busy days.
sents.vi: Năm 2024, thành phố bắt đầu thu phí vào cửa với khách trong ngày vào những ngày đông.

sents.t: Officials hope the fee will spread visitors more evenly across the year.
sents.vi: Chính quyền hy vọng mức phí sẽ phân bổ du khách đều hơn trong năm.

sents.t: Critics argue that the fee is too small to change tourists’ behaviour.
sents.vi: Những người phản đối cho rằng mức phí quá nhỏ để thay đổi hành vi du khách.

q.q: Venice receives far more visitors than it has residents.
The entrance fee applies to all visitors every day of the year.
The fee has already reduced visitor numbers by half.

gram.title: Describing proportions in pie charts
gram.rule: account for · make up · constitute · represent · a quarter / a third / the majority / a small minority · just under / just over
gram.note: Pie charts show parts of a whole, so focus on proportions rather than rises and falls (unless there are two years). Vary your verbs: accounted for, made up, represented. Turn percentages into fractions when they are close: 26% → just over a quarter; 48% → just under half; 70% → the vast majority.

lines.t: What are the benefits of international tourism?
lines.vi: Lợi ích của du lịch quốc tế là gì?

lines.t: Economically, it brings in a lot of revenue and creates jobs in hospitality. Culturally, it encourages exchange; when people meet each other face to face, stereotypes tend to break down.
lines.vi: Về kinh tế, nó mang lại nhiều doanh thu và tạo việc làm trong ngành dịch vụ lưu trú. Về văn hoá, nó thúc đẩy giao lưu; khi gặp nhau trực tiếp, định kiến thường mất dần.

lines.t: Can tourism damage local culture?
lines.vi: Du lịch có thể làm hỏng văn hoá địa phương không?

lines.t: Yes, if it isn’t managed. Traditions sometimes turn into performances just for visitors, and places become so commercialised that they lose their authentic character.
lines.vi: Có, nếu không được quản lý. Truyền thống đôi khi trở thành màn trình diễn chỉ cho du khách, và nơi đó thương mại hoá đến mức mất đi nét chân thực.

lines.t: How can tourism be made more sustainable?

lines.t: Governments could limit visitor numbers at heritage sites and support ecotourism, where the money stays in the local community. Tourists can also help by travelling outside peak season.
lines.vi: Chính phủ có thể giới hạn số khách ở các di sản và hỗ trợ du lịch sinh thái, nơi tiền ở lại với cộng đồng địa phương. Du khách cũng có thể góp phần bằng cách đi ngoài mùa cao điểm.

gram2.title: Talking about benefits and drawbacks
gram2.rule: One advantage / benefit of … is that … · The main drawback is … · On the positive side, … · A downside of … is …
gram2.note: Use noun phrases to organise ideas: The main benefit of tourism is that it creates jobs. After of, use a noun or -ing: the advantage of travelling. After is that, use a full clause. Balance positive and negative points in Part 3 to show a mature view.

cue.card: Describe a tourist attraction you visited that you would recommend.
points: what it is and where it is
and explain why you would recommend it
model: I’d recommend the Ban Gioc waterfall in Cao Bang province, right on the border between Vietnam and China. I went there with three friends two summers ago, during the rainy season, which is actually the best time because the water is at its strongest.

It’s a long trip — about seven hours by coach from Hanoi — but the journey itself is part of the experience, because the road winds through limestone mountains and rice terraces. When we arrived, we took a small bamboo raft right up to the bottom of the falls. The spray was so strong that we got completely soaked, but it was breathtaking. In the evening we stayed with a Tay family in a nearby village, who cooked us dinner and taught us a few words of their language.

I’d recommend it because it still feels authentic. Unlike some famous places, it hasn’t become a tourist trap yet: the entrance fee is reasonable and most of the money goes to local people. My only advice is to go soon, before mass tourism changes it.

write.prompt: The pie charts below show the purpose of visits to one country in 2005 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Purpose of visit       2005    2025
Holiday / leisure      52%     38%
Business               26%     18%
Visiting friends       12%     14%
Study                   6%     20%
Other                   4%     10%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (purpose of visits → reasons why people travelled to)
Overview: holidays were the main reason in both years but fell; study rose most dramatically
Body 1: holiday and business — the two that declined
Body 2: study, visiting friends and other — the ones that grew
model: The two pie charts compare the reasons why international visitors travelled to a particular country in 2005 and 2025.

Overall, holidays were the most common purpose of visits in both years, although their share declined. The most striking change was the rapid growth in visitors coming to study, while business travel became less significant.

In 2005, just over half of all visits (52%) were for holidays and leisure. Twenty years later, this proportion had fallen to 38%, but it still remained the largest category. Business trips followed a similar pattern, decreasing from just over a quarter of visits to 18%.

By contrast, the share of people visiting to study more than tripled, rising from only 6% to a fifth of all visits by 2025. Visits to friends and relatives increased slightly, from 12% to 14%, and the proportion of trips for other reasons also grew, from 4% to 10%.

lines.t: Did you like science subjects at school?

lines.t: Do you read about science now?

lines.t: Sometimes. I follow a few channels that explain new discoveries in simple language, especially anything about space or artificial intelligence.
lines.vi: Thỉnh thoảng. Tôi theo dõi vài kênh giải thích những khám phá mới bằng ngôn ngữ đơn giản, nhất là về vũ trụ hay trí tuệ nhân tạo.

lines.t: Should governments fund scientific research?

lines.t: Yes, because a lot of important research doesn’t make money quickly, so private companies won’t pay for it. Many breakthroughs, like the internet, started with government funding.

cue.card: Describe an invention that has changed people’s lives.
points: when it was invented or became popular
and explain how it has changed people’s lives
model: I’d like to talk about online maps, particularly navigation apps on smartphones. The technology existed earlier, but it only became really popular in my country around 2012, when cheap smartphones and mobile data spread.

People use them for far more than just finding directions. They check traffic before leaving home, look up opening hours, read reviews of restaurants and even share their live location with family members. Delivery riders and taxi drivers basically depend on them for their whole job.

They’ve changed our lives in several ways. Most obviously, getting lost has almost disappeared — my parents still talk about stopping to ask strangers for directions. They’ve also created thousands of jobs in delivery and ride-hailing. On the other hand, some research suggests that relying on navigation apps has weakened our natural sense of direction. I’ve definitely noticed that I can’t remember routes as well as I used to, so it’s a good example of an invention that has both benefits and drawbacks.

write.prompt: The diagram below shows how coffee beans are processed. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
write.data: Stages: 1 coffee cherries picked by hand → 2 cherries washed and pulp removed → 3 beans dried in the sun for 2–3 weeks → 4 outer skin removed (hulling) → 5 beans sorted by size and quality → 6 beans roasted at about 200°C → 7 beans cooled → 8a packed as whole beans  OR  8b ground and packed.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (how coffee beans are processed → the stages in producing coffee)
Overview: eight main stages, from picking to packing; two possible final products
Body 1: stages 1–4 — picking, washing, drying, hulling
Body 2: stages 5–8 — sorting, roasting, cooling, packing whole or ground
model: The diagram illustrates the stages involved in producing coffee, from picking the fruit to packing the finished product.
Overall, there are eight main stages in the process. It begins with harvesting coffee cherries by hand and ends with the beans being packed, either whole or after they have been ground.

First, ripe coffee cherries are picked by hand. They are then washed, and the soft pulp is removed so that only the beans remain. After that, the beans are spread out and dried in the sun for two to three weeks. Once they are completely dry, their outer skin is removed in a process known as hulling.

Next, the beans are sorted according to their size and quality. They are subsequently roasted at a temperature of around 200°C and then left to cool. Finally, the beans are packed. At this point there are two options: they can either be sold as whole beans or be ground into powder before packaging.

words.ex: Fathers now get two weeks of parental leave.
words.exVi: Các ông bố giờ được nghỉ hai tuần khi có con.

words.ex: Demand for nursing is growing.
words.exVi: Nhu cầu điều dưỡng đang tăng.

words.ex: Loneliness is a serious problem for older people.
words.exVi: Cô đơn là vấn đề nghiêm trọng với người già.

words.ex: Many young adults depend on their parents financially.
words.exVi: Nhiều người trẻ phụ thuộc tài chính vào bố mẹ.

words.vi: đạo hiếu, bổn phận làm con
words.ex: Filial duty is an important value in Asian cultures.
words.exVi: Đạo hiếu là giá trị quan trọng trong văn hoá châu Á.

words.ex: My grandmother passed on her recipes to me.
words.exVi: Bà tôi truyền lại công thức nấu ăn cho tôi.

lines.t: Do you live with your family?
lines.vi: Bạn có sống cùng gia đình không?

lines.t: Yes, in a multigenerational home — my parents, my grandmother, my wife and I. It’s a bit crowded, but it means someone is always there to help.
lines.vi: Có, trong một nhà nhiều thế hệ — bố mẹ, bà, vợ tôi và tôi. Hơi chật nhưng lúc nào cũng có người giúp đỡ.

lines.t: How often do you see your grandparents?
lines.vi: Bạn gặp ông bà thường xuyên không?

lines.t: Every day, since my grandmother lives with us. She’s eighty-five and still tells the best stories in the family.
lines.vi: Hằng ngày, vì bà sống cùng chúng tôi. Bà tám mươi lăm tuổi và vẫn kể chuyện hay nhất nhà.

lines.t: Is family more important to you now than when you were a child?
lines.vi: Gia đình có quan trọng với bạn hơn so với hồi bé không?

lines.t: I think so. As a child I took it for granted, but now I realise how much my parents sacrificed, so I try to spend more time with them.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ vậy. Hồi bé tôi coi đó là điều hiển nhiên, nhưng giờ tôi nhận ra bố mẹ đã hy sinh bao nhiêu, nên tôi cố dành nhiều thời gian hơn cho họ.

sents.t: Almost 30 per cent of people in Japan are now over 65, the highest proportion in the world.
sents.vi: Gần 30% dân số Nhật hiện trên 65 tuổi, tỉ lệ cao nhất thế giới.

sents.t: With a low birth rate, the working-age population has been shrinking since the 1990s.
sents.vi: Với tỉ lệ sinh thấp, dân số trong độ tuổi lao động đã giảm từ thập niên 1990.

sents.t: The government has responded by encouraging older people to keep working.
sents.vi: Chính phủ đã ứng phó bằng cách khuyến khích người già tiếp tục làm việc.

sents.t: Robots are also being tested in care homes to help staff lift and move residents.
sents.vi: Robot cũng đang được thử nghiệm ở viện dưỡng lão để giúp nhân viên nâng, di chuyển người cao tuổi.

sents.t: Nevertheless, there is still a serious shortage of nurses and caregivers.
sents.vi: Tuy vậy, vẫn thiếu nghiêm trọng điều dưỡng và người chăm sóc.

q.q: Japan has the highest proportion of over-65s in the world.
Japan’s working-age population started to grow in the 1990s.
Most Japanese care homes now use robots.

gram.title: Advantages–disadvantages essay structure
gram.rule: The main advantage is that … · Another benefit is … · However, this also has drawbacks. · Overall, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
gram.note: If the question asks “Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?”, you must give a clear answer. Write one body paragraph for each side, then explain in the conclusion which side is stronger and why. Use outweigh as a verb: the benefits outweigh the costs.

ex.t: The main advantage is that children grow up with grandparents.
ex.vi: Lợi ích chính là trẻ lớn lên cùng ông bà.

ex.t: Another benefit is lower childcare costs.
ex.vi: Một lợi ích khác là chi phí trông trẻ thấp hơn.

ex.t: However, this arrangement also has drawbacks.
ex.vi: Tuy nhiên, cách sắp xếp này cũng có hạn chế.

ex.t: In my view, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
ex.vi: Theo tôi, lợi ích lớn hơn bất lợi.

drill.t: The benefits ___ the drawbacks.
drill.vi: Lợi ích lớn hơn bất lợi.

drill.t: The main advantage is ___ costs are shared.
drill.vi: Lợi ích chính là chi phí được chia sẻ.

drill.t: ___ benefit is emotional support.
drill.vi: Một lợi ích khác là sự hỗ trợ tinh thần.

drill.t: This also has some ___.
drill.vi: Điều này cũng có vài hạn chế.

lines.t: Who should look after elderly people: families or the state?
lines.vi: Ai nên chăm sóc người già: gia đình hay nhà nước?

lines.t: Ideally both. In my culture filial duty is very strong, so families do most of the caring. But when someone needs professional nursing, families can’t do it alone, and the state should help.
lines.vi: Lý tưởng là cả hai. Trong văn hoá của tôi đạo hiếu rất mạnh nên gia đình chăm sóc là chính. Nhưng khi ai đó cần điều dưỡng chuyên nghiệp, gia đình không tự làm được, và nhà nước nên hỗ trợ.

lines.t: What can young people learn from older people?
lines.vi: Người trẻ học được gì từ người già?

lines.t: Patience, mainly, and a sense of perspective. My grandmother lived through a war, so when I complain about small problems at work, she reminds me what real difficulty looks like.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu là sự kiên nhẫn và cách nhìn nhận. Bà tôi đã sống qua chiến tranh, nên khi tôi than vãn chuyện nhỏ ở chỗ làm, bà nhắc tôi khó khăn thật sự là thế nào.

lines.t: Why are people having fewer children?
lines.vi: Vì sao người ta sinh ít con hơn?

lines.t: Mainly cost. Housing, education and childcare are so expensive that many couples feel they can only afford one child. Women also have more career opportunities now, so they tend to have children later.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu là chi phí. Nhà ở, giáo dục và trông trẻ đắt đến mức nhiều cặp vợ chồng thấy chỉ nuôi nổi một con. Phụ nữ giờ cũng có nhiều cơ hội nghề nghiệp hơn nên thường sinh con muộn hơn.

gram2.title: Gerunds as subjects and after prepositions
gram2.rule: Living with grandparents is … · instead of / without / by / after + -ing · be used to + -ing
gram2.note: An -ing form can be the subject of a sentence: Caring for elderly parents is demanding. After every preposition, use -ing, not to + verb: instead of moving, by working, without asking. Be used to + -ing means “be familiar with”, which is different from used to + verb (past habit).

ex.t: Caring for an elderly parent can be exhausting.
ex.vi: Chăm sóc cha mẹ già có thể rất mệt mỏi.

ex.t: Many couples delay having children.
ex.vi: Nhiều cặp vợ chồng trì hoãn việc sinh con.

ex.t: Instead of retiring, she started a business.
ex.vi: Thay vì nghỉ hưu, bà ấy mở một công việc kinh doanh.

ex.t: I’m used to living with a big family.
ex.vi: Tôi đã quen sống trong gia đình đông người.

drill.t: ___ in a big family teaches you to share.
drill.vi: Lớn lên trong gia đình đông người dạy bạn biết chia sẻ.

drill.t: He saved money by ___ with his parents.
drill.vi: Anh ấy tiết kiệm tiền bằng cách sống với bố mẹ.

drill.t: She is used to ___ early.
drill.vi: Cô ấy đã quen dậy sớm.

drill.t: They left without ___ goodbye.
drill.vi: Họ rời đi mà không chào tạm biệt.

cue.card: Describe an older person you enjoy spending time with.
points: and explain why you enjoy spending time with them
model: I’d like to talk about Mr Tuan, who lives in the flat next to mine. He’s a retired history teacher in his late seventies, and I got to know him about four years ago when I helped him carry some shopping upstairs.

Since then we’ve developed a kind of routine. Every Sunday morning I join him for tea on his balcony, and we play a game of Chinese chess, which he almost always wins. Sometimes I help him with his phone — he’s very keen to video-call his grandchildren in Germany — and in return he tells me about the history of our neighbourhood, like which buildings were here before the war.

I enjoy his company because he’s curious about everything and he never lectures me, even though he was a teacher for forty years. There’s obviously a generation gap — he thinks my generation spends too much time on screens — but we laugh about it. I also think it matters to him: his wife passed away a few years ago, and I know loneliness can be a real problem for older people living alone.

write.prompt: In many countries, more and more older people are living alone rather than with their families. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + answer (disadvantages outweigh, mainly because of loneliness and safety)
Body 1: advantages — independence, privacy, fewer family conflicts
Body 2: disadvantages — loneliness, health emergencies, cost of care
Conclusion: restate the answer and suggest a middle way (living nearby)
model: In many parts of the world, an increasing number of elderly people now live on their own instead of with their children. Although this arrangement offers some benefits, I believe its drawbacks, particularly loneliness and the risks to health, are more significant.

Living alone certainly has advantages. Many older people value their independence and prefer to organise their days in their own way, without having to adapt to the routines of a busy household. It also gives both generations more privacy, which can reduce the tension that sometimes arises when parents and adult children share a home. For those who are healthy and have an active social life, living independently can help them stay confident and mentally alert.

However, these benefits are outweighed by serious disadvantages. The most obvious is loneliness: older people who live alone may go for days without a proper conversation, and research has linked social isolation to depression and memory problems. Safety is another concern. If an elderly person falls or becomes ill at night, there may be nobody there to call for help. Finally, when they eventually need daily assistance, paying for professional care can be extremely expensive for families and governments.

In conclusion, while living alone allows older people to remain independent, the risks of isolation and unattended health emergencies are, in my view, greater. A sensible compromise may be for elderly parents to live close to their children, so that they can keep their independence while still receiving regular support.

units.title: Waste, energy & recycling
units.goal: Talk about environmental habits and policies, and compare two sets of data.

words.ex: Solar power is a form of renewable energy.
words.exVi: Điện mặt trời là một dạng năng lượng tái tạo.

words.ex: Coal and oil are fossil fuels.
words.exVi: Than và dầu là nhiên liệu hoá thạch.

words.ex: Most plastic ends up in landfill.
words.exVi: Phần lớn nhựa cuối cùng ở bãi chôn lấp.

words.ex: Single-use plastic bags are being banned.
words.exVi: Túi nhựa dùng một lần đang bị cấm.

words.ex: Biodegradable packaging breaks down naturally.
words.exVi: Bao bì phân huỷ sinh học tự phân rã.

words.ex: We compost our food waste.
words.exVi: Chúng tôi ủ phân từ rác thực phẩm.

words.ex: Carbon emissions must be cut by half.
words.exVi: Khí thải carbon phải được cắt giảm một nửa.

words.ex: We installed solar panels on our roof.
words.exVi: Chúng tôi lắp pin mặt trời trên mái nhà.

words.ex: A wind farm was built along the coast.
words.exVi: Một trang trại điện gió được xây dọc bờ biển.

words.ex: Energy-efficient bulbs last longer.
words.exVi: Bóng đèn tiết kiệm năng lượng bền hơn.

words.ex: Energy consumption peaks in summer.
words.exVi: Tiêu thụ năng lượng đạt đỉnh vào mùa hè.

words.ex: We need a more sustainable lifestyle.
words.exVi: Chúng ta cần lối sống bền vững hơn.

words.ex: Batteries must be disposed of safely.
words.exVi: Pin phải được xử lý an toàn.

words.ex: Tax incentives encourage people to buy electric cars.
words.exVi: Ưu đãi thuế khuyến khích mua xe điện.

words.ex: Half of household waste is food.
words.exVi: Một nửa rác sinh hoạt là thực phẩm.

words.ex: The dam generates electricity for the region.
words.exVi: Con đập sản xuất điện cho cả vùng.

words.ex: France relies heavily on nuclear power.
words.exVi: Pháp phụ thuộc nhiều vào năng lượng hạt nhân.

words.ex: In total, 40% of waste was recycled.
words.exVi: Tổng cộng 40% rác được tái chế.

words.ex: The figures were 20% and 35% respectively.
words.exVi: Các con số lần lượt là 20% và 35%.

words.ex: Coal power will be phased out by 2040.

lines.t: Do you recycle at home?
lines.vi: Bạn có tái chế ở nhà không?

lines.t: We try to. We separate plastic bottles and paper, and my mother composts vegetable waste for her plants. But honestly, I’m not sure everything we separate actually gets recycled.
lines.vi: Chúng tôi cố gắng. Chúng tôi tách chai nhựa và giấy, mẹ tôi ủ rau thừa làm phân bón cây. Nhưng thật lòng, tôi không chắc mọi thứ đã tách có thật sự được tái chế.

lines.t: Do you try to save energy?
lines.vi: Bạn có cố tiết kiệm năng lượng không?

lines.t: Yes, mostly to save money. I switch off the air conditioner when I leave a room, and we’ve replaced all our bulbs with energy-efficient ones.
lines.vi: Có, chủ yếu để tiết kiệm tiền. Tôi tắt điều hoà khi ra khỏi phòng, và chúng tôi đã thay toàn bộ bóng đèn bằng loại tiết kiệm năng lượng.

lines.t: Do you use a lot of plastic?
lines.vi: Bạn có dùng nhiều đồ nhựa không?

lines.t: More than I’d like. I carry a reusable bottle, but takeaway food comes with so much single-use packaging that it’s hard to avoid.
lines.vi: Nhiều hơn tôi muốn. Tôi mang bình nước dùng lại, nhưng đồ ăn mang về đi kèm quá nhiều bao bì dùng một lần nên khó tránh.

sents.t: The price of solar panels fell by around 90 per cent between 2010 and 2020.
sents.vi: Giá pin mặt trời giảm khoảng 90% từ năm 2010 đến 2020.

sents.t: In many sunny countries, solar is now the cheapest way to generate new electricity.
sents.vi: Ở nhiều nước nhiều nắng, điện mặt trời hiện là cách rẻ nhất để sản xuất điện mới.

sents.t: Vietnam installed more than 16,000 megawatts of solar capacity in just three years.
sents.vi: Việt Nam đã lắp đặt hơn 16.000 MW công suất điện mặt trời chỉ trong ba năm.

sents.t: However, the power grid was not ready, so some of this electricity could not be used.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, lưới điện chưa sẵn sàng nên một phần điện này không được sử dụng.

sents.t: Experts say that storage and grid investment are now as important as building new panels.
sents.vi: Chuyên gia nói đầu tư lưu trữ và lưới điện giờ quan trọng ngang xây thêm pin.

q.q: Solar panels became much cheaper between 2010 and 2020.
All of the electricity from Vietnam’s new solar farms was used.
Vietnam now produces more solar power than wind power.

gram.title: Giving and comparing figures
gram.rule: respectively · compared with · while / whereas · followed by · the figure for X · approximately / roughly / nearly
gram.note: When two data sets appear together, compare them in the same sentence instead of listing them one by one. Respectively matches figures to items in order: Germany and Spain recycled 60% and 40% respectively. Use approximately or nearly for rounded numbers, and the figure for … to avoid repeating nouns.

ex.t: Germany and Italy recycled 67% and 50% respectively.
ex.vi: Đức và Ý tái chế lần lượt 67% và 50%.

ex.t: The figure for France was slightly lower.
ex.vi: Con số của Pháp thấp hơn một chút.

ex.t: Coal was the main source, followed by gas.
ex.vi: Than là nguồn chính, sau đó là khí đốt.

ex.t: Nearly a third of waste went to landfill.
ex.vi: Gần một phần ba rác được đưa đến bãi chôn lấp.

drill.t: The UK and Spain produced 30 and 20 tonnes ___.
drill.vi: Anh và Tây Ban Nha lần lượt sản xuất 30 và 20 tấn.

drill.t: ___ for nuclear power was 10%.
drill.vi: Con số của điện hạt nhân là 10%.

drill.t: Wind was the largest source, ___ by solar.
drill.vi: Gió là nguồn lớn nhất, tiếp theo là mặt trời.

drill.t: Recycling rose to ___ 45%.
drill.vi: Tỉ lệ tái chế tăng lên xấp xỉ 45%.

lines.t: Who is more responsible for protecting the environment: individuals or governments?
lines.vi: Ai có trách nhiệm bảo vệ môi trường nhiều hơn: cá nhân hay chính phủ?

lines.t: Governments and large companies, in my opinion, because their decisions have a much bigger impact. One power station can produce more emissions than a whole city of people trying to save energy. But individual choices still send a message.
lines.vi: Theo tôi là chính phủ và các công ty lớn, vì quyết định của họ tác động lớn hơn nhiều. Một nhà máy điện có thể thải nhiều hơn cả một thành phố người dân cố tiết kiệm điện. Nhưng lựa chọn cá nhân vẫn tạo ra thông điệp.

lines.t: How can people be encouraged to recycle more?
lines.vi: Làm sao khuyến khích mọi người tái chế nhiều hơn?

lines.t: Make it easy and give incentives. In some countries you get money back when you return bottles, and recycling rates there are above ninety per cent. If people have to travel far to dispose of rubbish properly, they simply won’t.
lines.vi: Làm cho nó dễ dàng và có biện pháp khuyến khích. Ở một số nước, trả lại chai sẽ được hoàn tiền, và tỉ lệ tái chế ở đó trên chín mươi phần trăm. Nếu phải đi xa mới xử lý rác đúng cách, người ta sẽ không làm.

lines.t: Should fossil fuels be phased out completely?
lines.vi: Có nên loại bỏ hoàn toàn nhiên liệu hoá thạch không?

lines.t: Eventually, yes, but it has to be gradual. Developing countries still need cheap and reliable electricity, so rich countries should help them pay for renewable energy rather than just telling them to stop using coal.
lines.vi: Cuối cùng thì có, nhưng phải từ từ. Các nước đang phát triển vẫn cần điện rẻ và ổn định, nên nước giàu nên giúp họ chi trả cho năng lượng tái tạo thay vì chỉ bảo họ ngừng dùng than.

gram2.title: Making suggestions and recommendations
gram2.rule: should / ought to · It is essential that … · One way to … would be to … · suggest + -ing / suggest that + subject + verb
gram2.note: In Speaking and Writing, recommendations sound more natural when they are specific. After suggest, use -ing or a that-clause, never “suggest to do”: I suggest charging for plastic bags. It is essential / vital that + subject + base verb is formal and strong: It is essential that every city provide recycling bins.

ex.t: The government should invest in solar power.
ex.vi: Chính phủ nên đầu tư vào điện mặt trời.

ex.t: One way to reduce waste would be to charge for bags.
ex.vi: Một cách giảm rác là thu phí túi nilon.

ex.t: I suggest using public transport twice a week.
ex.vi: Tôi đề nghị đi phương tiện công cộng hai lần một tuần.

ex.t: It is essential that companies reduce packaging.
ex.vi: Điều thiết yếu là các công ty giảm bao bì.

drill.vi: Tôi đề nghị ăn ít thịt hơn.

drill.t: One way to save energy would be ___ lights.
drill.vi: Một cách tiết kiệm điện là tắt đèn.

drill.t: People ___ to reduce their plastic use.
drill.vi: Mọi người nên giảm dùng nhựa.

drill.t: It is essential that everyone ___.
drill.vi: Điều thiết yếu là mọi người đều tái chế.

cue.card: Describe something you do to help protect the environment.
points: how difficult or easy it is
and explain why you do it
model: One thing I do is avoid single-use plastic as much as I can, especially bags and drinking straws. I started about three years ago, after watching a documentary that showed how much plastic washes up on beaches in central Vietnam.

In practice, it means carrying a small kit with me: a cloth bag, a metal straw and a reusable water bottle. When I order coffee, I ask them to pour it into my bottle, and at the market I put vegetables straight into my bag. I also buy shampoo and washing-up liquid from a refill shop near my office.

Some parts are easy now that it’s become a habit, but takeaway food is still difficult, because almost every restaurant packs meals in plastic boxes. I do it partly because I genuinely don’t want to add to the landfill problem, and partly because I think small actions spread. Two of my colleagues started bringing their own bottles after seeing mine, so even if one person’s impact is small, it isn’t zero.

write.prompt: The table below shows how household waste was dealt with in four countries in 2022. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Country     Recycled   Composted   Burned for energy   Landfill
Germany     48%        19%         32%                 1%
UK          28%        16%         45%                11%
Italy       33%        20%         21%                26%
Greece      15%         6%          2%                77%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (dealt with → disposed of / methods of managing)
Overview: Germany relied least on landfill and recycled most; Greece sent most waste to landfill
Body 1: Germany and the UK — recycling vs burning for energy
Body 2: Italy and Greece — more landfill, much less burning
model: The table compares the methods that four European countries used to manage their household waste in 2022.

Overall, Germany had the most environmentally friendly system, recycling the highest share of its waste and sending almost none to landfill. Greece, by contrast, relied overwhelmingly on landfill and recycled the least.

Nearly half of Germany’s household waste (48%) was recycled and a further 19% was composted, while most of the remainder was burned to generate energy. Only 1% ended up in landfill. The UK also landfilled relatively little (11%), but it burned far more waste than any other country, at 45%, and recycled 28%.

Italy’s figures were more evenly distributed: it recycled a third of its waste and composted a fifth, but just over a quarter still went to landfill. Greece was very different from the other three countries. More than three quarters of its waste (77%) was buried in landfill, whereas recycling and composting accounted for only 15% and 6% respectively, and almost none was used for energy.

levels.name: Band 6→7
levels.title: Competent: abstract and global issues
levels.desc: Globalisation, public spending, art, artificial intelligence, language, housing, the media, wildlife, childhood and space — topics where you must explain ideas, not just describe them.
goals: Use less common vocabulary and collocations accurately (e.g. “widen the gap”, “a pressing concern”)
Write complex sentences with nominalisation, participle clauses and concession
Develop every body paragraph with a clear point, explanation and specific example
Speak at length in Part 3 with speculation, evaluation and comparison
Handle mixed Task 1 charts and select the key features instead of listing every number
extra: Cambridge IELTS 16–18: one full Reading test a week in 60 minutes, then analyse every wrong answer
Listen to a 10-minute podcast daily (BBC 6 Minute English → BBC Radio 4 “More or Less”) and shadow 2 minutes
Keep a collocation notebook: 10 new pairs a week, used in your own sentences
Have one Writing task a fortnight marked by a teacher against the four criteria

units.title: Globalisation
units.goal: Discuss the effects of globalisation on economies and cultures, using nominalisation and concession.

words.ex: Globalisation has connected markets around the world.
words.exVi: Toàn cầu hoá đã kết nối các thị trường trên thế giới.

words.ex: Multinationals employ millions of people in Asia.
words.exVi: Các công ty đa quốc gia tuyển hàng triệu lao động ở châu Á.

words.vi: thuê ngoài, chuyển việc ra nước ngoài
words.ex: Many firms outsource customer service.
words.exVi: Nhiều công ty thuê ngoài dịch vụ khách hàng.

words.ex: Free trade agreements reduce import taxes.
words.exVi: Hiệp định thương mại tự do giảm thuế nhập khẩu.

words.ex: Critics fear the homogenisation of culture.
words.exVi: Những người phê phán lo ngại sự đồng nhất hoá văn hoá.

words.ex: Language is central to cultural identity.
words.exVi: Ngôn ngữ là trung tâm của bản sắc văn hoá.

words.ex: National economies are increasingly interdependent.
words.exVi: Các nền kinh tế quốc gia ngày càng phụ thuộc lẫn nhau.

words.ex: The pandemic disrupted global supply chains.
words.exVi: Đại dịch làm gián đoạn chuỗi cung ứng toàn cầu.

words.ex: Some factories exploit cheap labour.
words.exVi: Một số nhà máy bóc lột lao động giá rẻ.

words.ex: Trade has raised the standard of living for millions.
words.exVi: Thương mại đã nâng mức sống của hàng triệu người.

words.ex: Globalisation may widen the gap between rich and poor.
words.exVi: Toàn cầu hoá có thể nới rộng khoảng cách giàu nghèo.

words.ex: Some job losses are inevitable.
words.exVi: Một số việc mất đi là không tránh khỏi.

words.ex: Foreign investment created new industrial zones.
words.exVi: Đầu tư nước ngoài tạo ra các khu công nghiệp mới.

words.ex: Protectionism is rising again in some countries.
words.exVi: Chủ nghĩa bảo hộ đang trỗi dậy ở một số nước.

words.ex: The government raised tariffs on imported steel.
words.exVi: Chính phủ tăng thuế quan với thép nhập khẩu.

words.ex: Globalisation has increased labour mobility.
words.exVi: Toàn cầu hoá làm tăng sự dịch chuyển lao động.

words.ex: A few tech giants dominate the market.
words.exVi: Vài gã khổng lồ công nghệ thống trị thị trường.

words.ex: Local traditions are slowly being eroded.
words.exVi: Truyền thống địa phương đang dần bị xói mòn.

words.ex: Exports brought prosperity to the region.
words.exVi: Xuất khẩu mang lại thịnh vượng cho khu vực.

words.ex: Globalisation is a double-edged sword.
words.exVi: Toàn cầu hoá là con dao hai lưỡi.

lines.t: Do you often buy products made in other countries?
lines.vi: Bạn có hay mua sản phẩm sản xuất ở nước khác không?

lines.t: All the time, often without realising it. My phone was designed in one country, assembled in another and probably contains parts from a dozen more.
lines.vi: Lúc nào cũng vậy, thường là không nhận ra. Điện thoại của tôi được thiết kế ở một nước, lắp ráp ở nước khác và có lẽ chứa linh kiện từ cả chục nước nữa.

lines.t: Do you prefer local or international food?
lines.vi: Bạn thích đồ ăn địa phương hay quốc tế?

lines.t: Local food on a daily basis, without a doubt. International chains are convenient, but they taste the same everywhere, which I find a bit dull.
lines.vi: Hằng ngày thì chắc chắn là đồ địa phương. Chuỗi quốc tế tiện, nhưng ở đâu vị cũng như nhau, tôi thấy hơi nhàm.

lines.t: Would you like to work for an international company?
lines.vi: Bạn có muốn làm cho công ty quốc tế không?

lines.t: I already do, in a sense — our main client is Japanese. I enjoy it because you pick up different ways of working, although time differences can be exhausting.
lines.vi: Theo một nghĩa nào đó thì tôi đang làm — khách hàng chính của chúng tôi là người Nhật. Tôi thích vì học được nhiều cách làm việc khác nhau, dù chênh lệch múi giờ có thể rất mệt.

read.title: Winners and losers of global trade

sents.t: Between 1990 and 2019, the share of the world’s population living in extreme poverty fell from 36 per cent to under 10 per cent.
sents.vi: Từ 1990 đến 2019, tỉ lệ dân số thế giới sống trong nghèo cùng cực giảm từ 36% xuống dưới 10%.

sents.t: Much of this improvement took place in East Asia, where export-led growth created millions of factory jobs.
sents.vi: Phần lớn sự cải thiện này diễn ra ở Đông Á, nơi tăng trưởng dựa vào xuất khẩu tạo ra hàng triệu việc làm nhà máy.

sents.t: At the same time, some manufacturing towns in wealthier countries lost their main employers.
sents.vi: Cùng lúc đó, một số thị trấn sản xuất ở các nước giàu hơn mất đi những nhà tuyển dụng chính.

sents.t: Economists generally agree that trade increases total wealth, but they disagree about how the gains should be shared.
sents.vi: Các nhà kinh tế nhìn chung đồng ý rằng thương mại làm tăng tổng của cải, nhưng bất đồng về việc nên chia lợi ích thế nào.

sents.t: Retraining programmes for displaced workers have produced mixed results.
sents.vi: Các chương trình đào tạo lại cho lao động mất việc cho kết quả không đồng đều.

q.q: Extreme poverty fell to less than a tenth of the world’s population by 2019.
Economists disagree about whether trade increases total wealth.
Retraining programmes have been most successful in Europe.

gram.title: Nominalisation: turning verbs into nouns
gram.rule: globalise → globalisation · grow → growth · decide → decision · The rapid growth of trade has led to …
gram.note: Academic writing often packs an idea into a noun phrase instead of a whole clause. Compare “Because trade has grown rapidly, …” with “The rapid growth of trade has …”. This sounds more formal and lets you put the main idea at the start of the sentence. Don’t overdo it — two or three nominalised phrases per paragraph is enough.

ex.t: The expansion of free trade has created jobs.
ex.vi: Sự mở rộng thương mại tự do đã tạo việc làm.

ex.t: The disappearance of local shops worries residents.
ex.vi: Sự biến mất của cửa hàng địa phương khiến cư dân lo lắng.

ex.t: The introduction of tariffs led to higher prices.
ex.vi: Việc áp thuế quan dẫn đến giá cao hơn.

ex.t: There has been a significant reduction in poverty.
ex.vi: Đã có sự giảm nghèo đáng kể.

drill.t: The ___ of foreign companies created jobs.
drill.vi: Sự xuất hiện của công ty nước ngoài tạo việc làm.

drill.t: There was a sharp ___ in exports.
drill.vi: Xuất khẩu tăng mạnh.

drill.t: The ___ to close the factory shocked workers.
drill.vi: Quyết định đóng cửa nhà máy làm công nhân sốc.

drill.t: The ___ of traditions is a concern.
drill.vi: Việc mất đi truyền thống là một mối lo.

lines.t: Is globalisation making cultures more similar?
lines.vi: Toàn cầu hoá có làm các nền văn hoá giống nhau hơn không?

lines.t: On the surface, yes — people in Hanoi and Madrid wear the same brands and watch the same series. But I’d argue that deeper things, like family values or how people celebrate festivals, change much more slowly. If anything, global exposure sometimes makes people more protective of their own traditions.
lines.vi: Bề ngoài thì có — người ở Hà Nội và Madrid mặc cùng thương hiệu, xem cùng loạt phim. Nhưng tôi cho rằng những thứ sâu xa hơn, như giá trị gia đình hay cách đón lễ hội, thay đổi chậm hơn nhiều. Thậm chí, tiếp xúc toàn cầu đôi khi khiến người ta trân trọng truyền thống của mình hơn.

lines.t: Who benefits most from globalisation?
lines.vi: Ai hưởng lợi nhiều nhất từ toàn cầu hoá?

lines.t: Consumers and highly skilled workers, generally. Products are cheaper and skilled people can work anywhere. The ones who lose out tend to be low-skilled workers in industries that move abroad, and unless governments support them, resentment builds up.
lines.vi: Nhìn chung là người tiêu dùng và lao động tay nghề cao. Hàng rẻ hơn và người giỏi có thể làm việc ở bất cứ đâu. Người chịu thiệt thường là lao động tay nghề thấp trong các ngành chuyển ra nước ngoài, và nếu chính phủ không hỗ trợ, sự bất mãn sẽ tích tụ.

lines.t: Do you think globalisation will continue?
lines.vi: Bạn nghĩ toàn cầu hoá có tiếp tục không?

lines.t: In a different form. After the pandemic, many companies realised their supply chains were too fragile, so we’re seeing production move closer to home. But digital globalisation — services, ideas, online work — seems likely to keep accelerating.
lines.vi: Theo hình thức khác. Sau đại dịch, nhiều công ty nhận ra chuỗi cung ứng quá mong manh, nên ta thấy sản xuất dời về gần hơn. Nhưng toàn cầu hoá số — dịch vụ, ý tưởng, làm việc trực tuyến — có vẻ sẽ tiếp tục tăng tốc.

gram2.title: Concession: despite, although, even though, while
gram2.rule: Despite / In spite of + noun / -ing · Although / Even though + clause · While it is true that …, … · Admittedly, …
gram2.note: Concession shows that you have considered the other side, which is essential for band 7 in Task Response. Despite is followed by a noun or -ing, never a full clause: Despite earning more, … or Despite the fact that they earn more, … Even though is stronger than although. Admittedly introduces a point you accept before you challenge it.

ex.t: Despite creating jobs, foreign factories can pollute rivers.
ex.vi: Dù tạo việc làm, nhà máy nước ngoài có thể làm ô nhiễm sông.

ex.t: Although trade has grown, inequality remains.
ex.vi: Dù thương mại tăng, bất bình đẳng vẫn còn.

ex.t: Even though prices are lower, quality has fallen.
ex.vi: Dù giá thấp hơn, chất lượng đã giảm.

ex.t: Admittedly, some traditions have been lost.
ex.vi: Phải thừa nhận rằng một số truyền thống đã mất.

drill.t: ___ the benefits, many people oppose free trade.
drill.vi: Bất chấp lợi ích, nhiều người phản đối thương mại tự do.

drill.t: ___ wages rose, workers felt insecure.
drill.vi: Dù lương tăng, người lao động vẫn thấy bất an.

drill.t: In spite ___ the risks, they invested abroad.
drill.vi: Bất chấp rủi ro, họ đầu tư ra nước ngoài.

drill.t: Despite ___ cheap, the product sold badly.
drill.vi: Dù rẻ, sản phẩm bán kém.

cue.card: Describe a foreign product that is popular in your country.
points: and explain why you think it is so popular
model: I’m going to talk about Korean skincare products, which have become incredibly popular in Vietnam over the past decade.

They originally come from South Korea, of course, but they’re now sold everywhere here — in shopping malls, on social media and even in small neighbourhood shops. The main customers are young women, but I’ve noticed that more and more men, including some of my colleagues, have started using them too, mostly sunscreen and simple moisturisers.

I think there are three reasons for their popularity. The first is the influence of Korean dramas and music, which have made Korean beauty standards very fashionable. The second is that the products are marketed cleverly: the packaging is cute, the prices are affordable, and influencers post detailed reviews, so buyers feel well informed. And the third reason is practical — they’re designed for a climate and skin types fairly similar to ours. Admittedly, the trend has its downsides: some people now spend a lot of money on ten-step routines they don’t really need. But overall it’s a good example of how globalisation spreads culture through everyday consumer goods.

write.prompt: Some people think that globalisation has more negative effects than positive effects on developing countries. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + position (disagree overall: benefits greater, but costs real and need managing)
Body 1: concede the negatives — exploitation, environmental damage, cultural erosion, with a specific example
Body 2: main argument — poverty reduction, technology transfer, jobs for women; East Asia example
Conclusion: restate the position and the condition (strong regulation)
model: It is often claimed that developing nations lose more than they gain from globalisation. Although its costs are real and sometimes severe, I largely disagree with this view, since the integration of these countries into the world economy has been the main driver of the dramatic reduction in poverty over the past three decades.

Admittedly, globalisation has brought significant problems. In the rush to attract foreign investment, some governments have tolerated poor working conditions and weak environmental standards, and the collapse of a garment factory in Bangladesh in 2013, which killed more than a thousand workers, showed the human cost of this approach. There is also a risk that the spread of global brands and media erodes local languages and traditions, particularly among young people in cities.

Nevertheless, the benefits have been considerably greater. The expansion of export industries in countries such as Vietnam and China has lifted hundreds of millions of people out of extreme poverty, giving families a stable income for the first time. Foreign companies have also brought technology and management skills that local firms have since adopted, while factory work has given many women financial independence. Moreover, cheaper imported goods, from medicines to mobile phones, have raised the standard of living for ordinary households.

In conclusion, while globalisation undoubtedly carries risks for developing countries, I believe its positive effects, above all the large-scale reduction in poverty, outweigh the negative ones. The key challenge for governments is not to resist globalisation but to regulate it so that growth does not come at the expense of workers’ safety or the environment.

units.title: Public money & public services
units.goal: Debate how governments should spend money, using cleft sentences and the language of priority.

words.ex: Public spending on health rose by 8%.
words.exVi: Chi tiêu công cho y tế tăng 8%.

words.ex: Taxpayers expect value for money.
words.exVi: Người nộp thuế mong tiền được dùng hiệu quả.

words.ex: The budget allocates more money to schools.
words.exVi: Ngân sách phân bổ nhiều tiền hơn cho trường học.

words.ex: The state subsidises public transport.
words.exVi: Nhà nước trợ giá giao thông công cộng.

words.ex: The welfare system supports the unemployed.
words.exVi: Hệ thống phúc lợi hỗ trợ người thất nghiệp.

words.ex: Healthcare should be the top priority.
words.exVi: Y tế nên là ưu tiên hàng đầu.

words.ex: The metro is the city’s biggest infrastructure project.
words.exVi: Metro là dự án hạ tầng lớn nhất thành phố.

words.ex: Should the government fund the arts?
words.exVi: Chính phủ có nên tài trợ cho nghệ thuật?

words.ex: Politicians must be accountable to voters.
words.exVi: Chính trị gia phải chịu trách nhiệm trước cử tri.

words.ex: The railways were privatised in the 1990s.
words.exVi: Đường sắt được tư nhân hoá vào thập niên 1990.

words.ex: Support is means-tested, so only poorer families receive it.
words.exVi: Trợ cấp xét theo thu nhập nên chỉ gia đình nghèo được nhận.

words.ex: An ageing population is a growing burden on the state.
words.exVi: Dân số già là gánh nặng ngày càng lớn cho nhà nước.

words.ex: Prevention is more cost-effective than treatment.
words.exVi: Phòng ngừa hiệu quả chi phí hơn điều trị.

words.ex: Revenue from taxes fell during the crisis.
words.exVi: Nguồn thu từ thuế giảm trong khủng hoảng.

words.ex: We must invest in teachers, not just buildings.
words.exVi: Ta phải đầu tư vào giáo viên, không chỉ toà nhà.

words.ex: Education brings long-term benefits.
words.exVi: Giáo dục mang lại lợi ích dài hạn.

words.ex: Cutting research funding is short-sighted.
words.exVi: Cắt giảm kinh phí nghiên cứu là thiển cận.

words.vi: đánh đổi bằng, gây thiệt cho
words.ex: The stadium was built at the expense of local schools.
words.exVi: Sân vận động được xây với cái giá là các trường học địa phương.

words.ex: Safety should take precedence over profit.
words.exVi: An toàn nên được ưu tiên hơn lợi nhuận.

words.ex: Resources are scarce, so choices must be made.
words.exVi: Nguồn lực khan hiếm nên phải lựa chọn.

lines.t: What public facilities do you use most?
lines.vi: Bạn dùng tiện ích công cộng nào nhiều nhất?

lines.t: Probably the parks and the public library near my office. The library was renovated last year and it’s now one of the few quiet places in the city centre where you can work for free.
lines.vi: Có lẽ là công viên và thư viện công cộng gần cơ quan. Thư viện được cải tạo năm ngoái và giờ là một trong số ít nơi yên tĩnh ở trung tâm mà bạn làm việc miễn phí được.

lines.t: Are there enough public facilities where you live?
lines.vi: Nơi bạn sống có đủ tiện ích công cộng không?

lines.t: Not really. What we lack most is green space. New apartment blocks keep going up, but parks and playgrounds haven’t kept pace with the population.
lines.vi: Không hẳn. Thứ chúng tôi thiếu nhất là không gian xanh. Chung cư mới cứ mọc lên, nhưng công viên và sân chơi không theo kịp dân số.

lines.t: Would you pay more tax for better services?
lines.vi: Bạn có sẵn sàng đóng thuế cao hơn để có dịch vụ tốt hơn không?

lines.t: I would, as long as I could see where the money goes. People don’t mind paying tax nearly as much as they mind feeling it’s being wasted.
lines.vi: Có, miễn là tôi thấy được tiền đi đâu. Người ta không ngại đóng thuế bằng việc cảm thấy tiền bị lãng phí.

sents.t: A study of public health programmes in high-income countries estimated that every dollar spent on prevention saved an average of fourteen dollars.
sents.vi: Một nghiên cứu về chương trình y tế công ở các nước thu nhập cao ước tính mỗi đô la chi cho phòng ngừa tiết kiệm trung bình mười bốn đô la.

sents.t: Programmes such as tobacco taxes and childhood vaccination gave the highest returns.
sents.vi: Các chương trình như thuế thuốc lá và tiêm chủng cho trẻ em mang lại lợi ích cao nhất.

sents.t: Despite this, prevention typically receives less than five per cent of health budgets.
sents.vi: Dù vậy, phòng ngừa thường chỉ nhận chưa đến 5% ngân sách y tế.

sents.t: One explanation is political: the benefits appear years later, long after the next election.
sents.vi: Một cách giải thích mang tính chính trị: lợi ích xuất hiện nhiều năm sau, lâu sau kỳ bầu cử tới.

sents.t: Hospitals, by contrast, produce visible results that voters can see immediately.
sents.vi: Ngược lại, bệnh viện tạo ra kết quả hữu hình mà cử tri thấy ngay.

q.q: Prevention programmes saved more money than they cost.
Prevention usually receives about a quarter of health budgets.
Vaccination programmes were more cost-effective than tobacco taxes.

gram.title: Cleft sentences for emphasis
gram.rule: What + clause + is/was … (What we need is …) · It is/was … that/who … (It is the government that …) · The reason why … is that …
gram.note: Cleft sentences split one idea into two parts to highlight the key information. They are very natural in Speaking Part 3 and useful in essays for emphasis: What concerns me most is … / It is not the cost but the lack of planning that … Use them occasionally; one or two per answer is enough.

ex.t: What the city needs is more affordable housing.
ex.vi: Điều thành phố cần là thêm nhà ở giá phải chăng.

ex.t: It is the poorest families who suffer most.
ex.vi: Chính các gia đình nghèo nhất chịu thiệt nhiều nhất.

ex.t: The reason why prevention is ignored is that results take years.
ex.vi: Lý do phòng ngừa bị bỏ qua là kết quả cần nhiều năm.

ex.t: What surprised me was how little was spent on parks.
ex.vi: Điều làm tôi ngạc nhiên là chi cho công viên ít đến thế.

drill.t: ___ we lack is good public transport.
drill.vi: Thứ chúng ta thiếu là giao thông công cộng tốt.

drill.t: It is teachers ___ make schools work.
drill.vi: Chính giáo viên làm nên trường học.

drill.t: The reason ___ taxes rose is the war.
drill.vi: Lý do thuế tăng là chiến tranh.

drill.t: It was in 2010 ___ the bridge opened.
drill.vi: Chính năm 2010 cây cầu thông xe.

lines.t: Should governments spend money on the arts when there are poor people?
lines.vi: Chính phủ có nên chi tiền cho nghệ thuật khi vẫn còn người nghèo?

lines.t: I think it’s a false choice. Arts funding is usually a tiny fraction of the budget, and cutting it wouldn’t solve poverty. What’s more, museums and festivals bring in tourism and jobs. That said, basic needs like healthcare must clearly take precedence when resources are scarce.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ đó là lựa chọn giả. Kinh phí nghệ thuật thường chỉ là phần nhỏ ngân sách, cắt đi cũng không giải quyết được nghèo đói. Hơn nữa, bảo tàng và lễ hội mang lại du lịch và việc làm. Dù vậy, nhu cầu cơ bản như y tế rõ ràng phải được ưu tiên khi nguồn lực khan hiếm.

lines.t: Is it better for services to be run by the state or by private companies?
lines.vi: Dịch vụ nên do nhà nước hay công ty tư nhân điều hành?

lines.t: It depends on the service. Where there’s real competition, like telecoms, private firms tend to be more efficient. But for natural monopolies such as water or railways, privatisation has often meant higher prices without better quality, so I’d keep those public.
lines.vi: Còn tuỳ dịch vụ. Nơi có cạnh tranh thực sự như viễn thông, công ty tư nhân thường hiệu quả hơn. Nhưng với độc quyền tự nhiên như nước hay đường sắt, tư nhân hoá thường đồng nghĩa giá cao hơn mà chất lượng không tốt hơn, nên tôi sẽ giữ chúng công lập.

lines.t: Why do governments often focus on short-term projects?
lines.vi: Vì sao chính phủ hay tập trung vào dự án ngắn hạn?

lines.t: Mainly because of elections. A new bridge can be opened before the next vote, whereas the benefits of better teacher training appear ten years later. It’s short-sighted, but it’s politically rational.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu vì bầu cử. Một cây cầu mới có thể khánh thành trước kỳ bỏ phiếu, còn lợi ích của việc đào tạo giáo viên tốt hơn mười năm sau mới thấy. Điều đó thiển cận nhưng hợp lý về mặt chính trị.

gram2.title: The language of priorities
gram2.rule: should take priority / precedence over · rather than · at the expense of · come first · be more pressing than
gram2.note: Many Task 2 questions ask what governments should prioritise. Show your ranking clearly and explain why. Take priority over and at the expense of are followed by a noun or -ing. Rather than can join two verbs in the same form: invest in schools rather than build stadiums.

ex.t: Healthcare should take priority over defence.
ex.vi: Y tế nên được ưu tiên hơn quốc phòng.

ex.t: The city invested in roads rather than public transport.
ex.vi: Thành phố đầu tư đường sá thay vì giao thông công cộng.

ex.t: Growth came at the expense of the environment.
ex.vi: Tăng trưởng đến với cái giá là môi trường.

ex.t: Housing is a more pressing problem than tourism.
ex.vi: Nhà ở là vấn đề cấp bách hơn du lịch.

cue.card: Describe a public service or facility that you think needs improving.
points: and explain how it could be improved
model: I’d like to talk about the public bus network in my city, which I use three or four times a week, mainly to get to work when it’s raining too hard to ride my motorbike.

In fairness, it’s improved in some ways — the buses are newer and most of them have air conditioning now. But it still has three big problems. The first is reliability: there’s no way of knowing when a bus will actually arrive, so you can wait five minutes or forty. The second is that buses get stuck in exactly the same traffic as everyone else, so they’re rarely faster than a car. And the third is the stops themselves, many of which have no shelter and are blocked by parked motorbikes.

What would make the biggest difference, I think, is dedicated bus lanes on the main roads, because if buses were genuinely faster, people would switch voluntarily. Real-time arrival information on an app would also be cheap and very effective. It’s frustrating, because a better bus system would cost far less than new flyovers, but flyovers are more visible, so they tend to get the money.

write.prompt: Some people believe that governments should spend money on improving public services such as healthcare and education rather than on arts and culture. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both views + position (essential services first, but a modest arts budget is justified)
Body 1: the case for prioritising services — scarce resources, life and death, equality
Body 2: the case for arts funding — identity, tourism revenue, market failure; small cost
Conclusion: balance, with the condition that core services are adequately funded first
model: There is considerable debate about whether public money should go exclusively to essential services, such as hospitals and schools, or whether part of it should also support the arts. In my opinion, healthcare and education must come first, but a modest investment in culture is still justified because of the wider benefits it brings.

Those who argue that services should take priority have a strong case. Public funds are limited, and every dollar spent on a theatre is a dollar not spent on medicines or teachers. In many countries hospitals remain overcrowded and rural schools lack basic equipment, so it can seem irresponsible to fund an orchestra while these needs are unmet. Furthermore, essential services benefit the whole population, whereas audiences for opera or galleries tend to be wealthier and better educated.

On the other hand, there are convincing reasons for supporting culture. The arts help to preserve a nation’s identity and pass on its history to younger generations, something the market alone will not do, since traditional crafts and performances are rarely profitable. Cultural institutions can also generate significant revenue: museums and festivals attract tourists, who spend money in hotels and restaurants and create jobs. Crucially, arts budgets are usually tiny compared with health or education spending, so eliminating them would make almost no difference to the quality of those services.

In conclusion, while I agree that governments should prioritise the services that people depend on, I do not believe this requires abandoning the arts altogether. Provided that healthcare and education are adequately funded, spending a small proportion of the budget on culture is a reasonable investment in a society’s identity and economy.

units.title: Art & creativity
units.goal: Talk about art, creativity and its value, using participle clauses and dependent prepositions.

words.ex: Schools should encourage creativity.
words.exVi: Trường học nên khuyến khích sáng tạo.

lines.t: Do you like art?
lines.vi: Bạn có thích nghệ thuật không?

lines.t: I do, though I’m more into photography and street art than traditional painting. There’s something about art you can see for free, on a wall in your own neighbourhood, that appeals to me.
lines.vi: Có, dù tôi thích nhiếp ảnh và nghệ thuật đường phố hơn hội hoạ truyền thống. Nghệ thuật bạn xem miễn phí trên bức tường ngay khu mình ở có điều gì đó cuốn hút tôi.

lines.t: Did you learn art at school?
lines.vi: Bạn có học mỹ thuật ở trường không?

lines.t: Only until about twelve. After that it was dropped to make room for exam subjects, which I think was a pity, because it was the only lesson where there was no single right answer.
lines.vi: Chỉ đến khoảng mười hai tuổi. Sau đó môn này bị bỏ để nhường chỗ cho các môn thi, điều tôi thấy tiếc, vì đó là tiết duy nhất không có một đáp án đúng duy nhất.

lines.t: Have you been to an art gallery recently?
lines.vi: Gần đây bạn có đi phòng tranh không?

lines.t: Yes, a photography exhibition about the old quarter. Seeing photos of my own city from the 1930s was surprisingly moving.
lines.vi: Có, một triển lãm ảnh về phố cổ. Xem ảnh thành phố của chính mình từ thập niên 1930 cảm động một cách bất ngờ.

sents.t: In 2022, an image created with an AI program won first prize in a digital art competition in the United States.
sents.vi: Năm 2022, một bức ảnh tạo bằng chương trình AI giành giải nhất một cuộc thi nghệ thuật số ở Mỹ.

sents.t: The decision provoked angry reactions from artists, who argued that the winner had not really made anything.
sents.vi: Quyết định này gây phản ứng gay gắt từ các nghệ sĩ, những người cho rằng người thắng thực ra không làm ra gì cả.

sents.t: The winner replied that he had spent more than eighty hours refining his instructions to the program.
sents.vi: Người thắng đáp lại rằng anh đã mất hơn tám mươi giờ để tinh chỉnh lời nhắc cho chương trình.

sents.t: Some philosophers suggest that creativity requires intention and experience, which machines lack.
sents.vi: Một số triết gia cho rằng sáng tạo đòi hỏi ý định và trải nghiệm, thứ máy móc không có.

sents.t: Others point out that photography was also dismissed as mechanical when it was first invented.
sents.vi: Số khác chỉ ra rằng nhiếp ảnh cũng từng bị coi là máy móc khi mới ra đời.

q.q: The AI-generated image won a prize in a competition.
Artists welcomed the competition’s decision.
The competition later changed its rules about AI.

gram.title: Participle clauses
gram.rule: -ing clause (active): Walking through the gallery, I … · -ed clause (passive): Painted in 1889, the picture … · Having + past participle (earlier action)
gram.note: Participle clauses make writing more concise and varied. The subject of the participle must be the same as the subject of the main clause: Painted in 1889, the picture is … (the picture was painted). A wrong subject gives a “dangling participle”: ✗ Walking into the room, the painting caught my eye. Having + past participle shows the first action finished before the second.

ex.t: Built in the 11th century, the temple is the oldest in the city.
ex.vi: Được xây từ thế kỷ 11, ngôi đền lâu đời nhất thành phố.

ex.t: Using only recycled materials, the artist created a huge sculpture.
ex.vi: Chỉ dùng vật liệu tái chế, nghệ sĩ tạo ra một tác phẩm điêu khắc khổng lồ.

ex.t: Having studied in Paris, she returned to open a gallery.
ex.vi: Sau khi học ở Paris, cô ấy trở về mở phòng tranh.

ex.t: Paintings created by children are often very original.
ex.vi: Tranh do trẻ em vẽ thường rất độc đáo.

drill.t: ___ in 1920, the theatre needs repairs.
drill.vi: Được xây năm 1920, nhà hát cần sửa chữa.

drill.t: ___ the exhibition, I bought a catalogue.
drill.vi: Sau khi xem triển lãm, tôi mua một cuốn catalogue.

drill.t: Artists ___ in the city struggle to pay rent.
drill.vi: Nghệ sĩ sống ở thành phố khó trả tiền thuê nhà.

drill.t: ___ by the sea, she painted waves.
drill.vi: Được biển truyền cảm hứng, cô ấy vẽ sóng.

lines.t: Why do people value art?
lines.vi: Vì sao con người coi trọng nghệ thuật?

lines.t: I think it does something that information can’t. A news report can tell you a war happened, but a novel or a painting can make you feel what it was like. It also connects us across time — we can look at a two-thousand-year-old pot and recognise someone who cared about beauty, just like us.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ nó làm được điều mà thông tin không làm được. Bản tin cho bạn biết chiến tranh đã xảy ra, nhưng tiểu thuyết hay bức tranh khiến bạn cảm nhận được nó ra sao. Nó còn kết nối ta qua thời gian — nhìn chiếc bình hai nghìn năm tuổi, ta nhận ra một người cũng quan tâm đến cái đẹp như mình.

lines.t: Should art be a compulsory subject at school?
lines.vi: Mỹ thuật có nên là môn bắt buộc không?

lines.t: At least until the mid-teens, yes. It’s not about producing artists; it’s about developing creativity and the confidence to try things without a fixed answer, which employers increasingly say they want.
lines.vi: Ít nhất đến giữa tuổi thiếu niên thì có. Không phải để tạo ra nghệ sĩ, mà để phát triển sự sáng tạo và tự tin thử nghiệm khi không có đáp án cố định, điều mà nhà tuyển dụng ngày càng nói họ cần.

lines.t: Will AI replace human artists?
lines.vi: AI có thay thế nghệ sĩ không?

lines.t: It will probably replace some commercial work, like simple illustrations for adverts. But people care about the story behind a work — who made it and why — so I suspect human-made art will become more valued, not less, in the same way handmade furniture is worth more than factory-made.
lines.vi: Có lẽ nó sẽ thay thế một phần công việc thương mại, như minh hoạ đơn giản cho quảng cáo. Nhưng người ta quan tâm câu chuyện đằng sau tác phẩm — ai làm và vì sao — nên tôi đoán nghệ thuật do người làm sẽ được coi trọng hơn, giống như đồ gỗ thủ công đắt hơn đồ nhà máy.

gram2.title: Dependent prepositions

gram2.note: Many adjectives, verbs and nouns are followed by a fixed preposition, and errors with them are very common at band 6. Learn them as chunks. After a preposition, use a noun or -ing: capable of producing, contribute to improving (here to is a preposition).

drill.vi: Bảo tàng đóng góp cho du lịch.

cue.card: Describe a piece of art you have seen that you liked.
points: and explain why you liked it
model: The piece I’d like to describe is a large lacquer painting I saw at the Fine Arts Museum in Hanoi. It was painted in the 1930s by Nguyen Gia Tri, one of the artists who turned lacquer — which had been used mainly for decorating furniture — into a serious art form.

It shows a group of young women in a garden, but it’s not realistic at all. The figures are almost floating against a deep black background, and the colours are gold, red and a kind of eggshell white that seems to glow when you walk past, because the light catches the different layers. Made using dozens of layers of resin, each one polished by hand, it apparently took years to finish.

I liked it for two reasons. First, I was impressed by the sheer craftsmanship — you can’t really appreciate it from a photo, because the surface changes depending on where you stand. And second, I liked the idea behind it: taking a traditional Vietnamese craft and using it to create something completely modern. Having seen it, I started paying much more attention to lacquerware in ordinary shops, so it genuinely changed how I look at everyday objects.

write.prompt: The charts below show the number of visitors to three types of cultural venue in a city and the main reasons visitors gave for attending in 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Annual visitors (thousands)   2013   2023
Art museums                   420    610
Theatres                      380    290
Music festivals               150    540

Main reason for attending (2023, % of visitors)
Socialising with friends   41%
Interest in the art form   33%
Tourism / sightseeing      18%
Education / school trip     8%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both charts in one sentence
Overview: festivals and museums grew while theatres declined; socialising was the top reason
Body 1: visitor numbers — festivals more than tripled, museums up by nearly half, theatres down
Body 2: reasons — socialising vs interest, tourism and education; link to festival growth
model: The bar chart compares the number of people who visited three kinds of cultural venue in a city in 2013 and 2023, while the pie chart shows the main reasons that visitors gave for attending in 2023.

Overall, attendance at music festivals and art museums rose over the decade, whereas theatres became less popular. In 2023, the most common motivation for attending cultural events was social rather than artistic.

Music festivals experienced the most dramatic growth, with visitor numbers more than tripling from 150,000 to 540,000. Art museums remained the most visited venue, attracting 610,000 people in 2023, an increase of almost half compared with 2013. Theatres, by contrast, were the only venue to lose visitors, with numbers falling from 380,000 to 290,000, which meant they had changed from the second most popular venue to the least popular.

As for motivation, 41% of visitors said they attended mainly to spend time with friends, compared with a third who were primarily interested in the art form itself. Tourism accounted for just under a fifth of visits, and only 8% of visitors were attending for educational reasons, such as school trips. The prominence of socialising may partly explain the rapid rise in festival attendance.

units.title: Artificial intelligence
units.goal: Discuss the opportunities and risks of AI, using future forms and advanced hedging.

words.ex: The algorithm recommends videos you might like.
words.exVi: Thuật toán gợi ý video bạn có thể thích.

words.ex: Machine learning finds patterns in huge datasets.

words.vi: tình thế khó xử về đạo đức
words.ex: Self-driving cars raise ethical dilemmas.

words.ex: Over-reliance on AI may weaken our skills.

words.ex: Teachers will not be replaced in the foreseeable future.
words.exVi: Giáo viên sẽ không bị thay thế trong tương lai gần.

lines.t: Do you use any AI tools?
lines.vi: Bạn có dùng công cụ AI nào không?

lines.t: Yes, quite a lot now. I use one to summarise long reports and another to check my English emails. It saves time, although I always read the result carefully because it sometimes gets details wrong.
lines.vi: Có, giờ khá nhiều. Tôi dùng một công cụ để tóm tắt báo cáo dài và một cái khác để kiểm tra email tiếng Anh. Nó tiết kiệm thời gian, dù tôi luôn đọc kỹ kết quả vì đôi khi nó sai chi tiết.

lines.t: Has technology made your job easier?
lines.vi: Công nghệ có làm công việc của bạn dễ hơn không?

lines.t: Easier in some ways, harder in others. Calculations that took a day now take minutes, but clients expect answers much faster, so the pressure hasn’t really gone down.
lines.vi: Dễ hơn ở mặt này, khó hơn ở mặt khác. Tính toán từng mất cả ngày giờ chỉ vài phút, nhưng khách hàng mong câu trả lời nhanh hơn nhiều, nên áp lực không thực sự giảm.

lines.t: Is there any technology you would like to have?
lines.vi: Có công nghệ nào bạn muốn có không?

lines.t: A really good real-time translator. If I could speak to anyone in their own language, I’d travel much more adventurously.
lines.vi: Một máy dịch tức thời thật tốt. Nếu nói chuyện được với bất kỳ ai bằng tiếng của họ, tôi sẽ đi du lịch mạo hiểm hơn nhiều.

sents.t: In 2018, a large technology company stopped using an AI system that it had built to screen job applications.
sents.vi: Năm 2018, một công ty công nghệ lớn ngừng dùng hệ thống AI mà họ xây dựng để sàng lọc hồ sơ xin việc.

sents.t: The system had been trained on ten years of past applications, most of which came from men.
sents.vi: Hệ thống được huấn luyện trên hồ sơ của mười năm trước, phần lớn đến từ nam giới.

sents.t: As a result, it learned to give lower scores to CVs that mentioned women’s organisations.
sents.vi: Kết quả là nó học cách chấm điểm thấp hơn cho CV có nhắc đến tổ chức của phụ nữ.

sents.t: Engineers tried to correct the problem but could not guarantee that other biases would not appear.
sents.vi: Các kỹ sư cố sửa lỗi nhưng không thể đảm bảo các thiên lệch khác sẽ không xuất hiện.

sents.t: The case is now widely cited as an example of how AI can repeat human prejudice on a large scale.
sents.vi: Trường hợp này giờ được dẫn chứng rộng rãi như ví dụ về việc AI có thể lặp lại định kiến của con người trên quy mô lớn.

q.q: The AI system was trained mainly on applications from men.
Engineers successfully removed all bias from the system.
The company was fined because of the system.

gram.title: Future continuous and future perfect
gram.rule: will be + -ing (in progress at a future time) · will have + past participle (completed before a future time) · By 2040, …
gram.note: The future perfect is very useful for predictions with a deadline: By 2035, AI will have transformed most office jobs. The future continuous describes a situation in progress at a future moment: In ten years, many of us will be working alongside AI assistants. Both make Part 3 predictions sound more precise.

ex.t: By 2030, AI will have replaced many routine tasks.
ex.vi: Đến năm 2030, AI sẽ đã thay thế nhiều việc lặp lại.

ex.t: In twenty years, doctors will be using AI every day.
ex.vi: Hai mươi năm nữa, bác sĩ sẽ đang dùng AI hằng ngày.

ex.t: By the time my children grow up, self-driving cars will have become normal.
ex.vi: Khi con tôi lớn lên, xe tự lái sẽ đã trở nên bình thường.

ex.t: This time next year, I will be studying data science.
ex.vi: Giờ này năm sau tôi sẽ đang học khoa học dữ liệu.

drill.t: By 2040, robots ___ most factory work.
