words.ex: Local communities are the custodians of tradition.
words.exVi: Cộng đồng địa phương là người gìn giữ truyền thống.

words.ex: The poem has enduring popularity.
words.exVi: Bài thơ được yêu thích bền lâu.

words.ex: Many want to preserve the house, but few can afford to do so.
words.exVi: Nhiều người muốn giữ ngôi nhà nhưng ít ai đủ tiền làm như vậy.

lines.t: What traditional festivals do you celebrate?
lines.vi: Bạn đón những lễ hội truyền thống nào?

lines.t: Tet is the big one, of course. We still follow most of the customs — cleaning the house, visiting the graves of our ancestors, and giving lucky money — though the celebrations are shorter than in my grandparents’ day.
lines.vi: Tết là lớn nhất, đương nhiên. Chúng tôi vẫn giữ phần lớn phong tục — dọn nhà, viếng mộ tổ tiên, mừng tuổi — dù lễ ngắn hơn thời ông bà tôi.

lines.t: Do young people in your country value traditions?
lines.vi: Người trẻ ở nước bạn có coi trọng truyền thống không?

lines.t: More than people assume, actually. There’s been a real revival of interest in things like áo dài and traditional music, partly thanks to social media, although it’s sometimes more about style than meaning.
lines.vi: Thực ra nhiều hơn người ta nghĩ. Có sự hồi sinh thật sự trong quan tâm đến áo dài và âm nhạc truyền thống, một phần nhờ mạng xã hội, dù đôi khi thiên về phong cách hơn là ý nghĩa.

lines.t: Have you ever visited a historical site?
lines.vi: Bạn đã bao giờ thăm di tích lịch sử chưa?

lines.t: Many times. My favourite is the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, where students still go to pray before exams, which I find quite touching.
lines.vi: Nhiều lần. Tôi thích nhất Văn Miếu ở Hà Nội, nơi học sinh vẫn đến cầu may trước kỳ thi, điều tôi thấy khá cảm động.

sents.t: Many major European museums hold objects that were taken from other countries during the colonial period.
sents.vi: Nhiều bảo tàng lớn ở châu Âu đang giữ hiện vật được lấy từ các nước khác trong thời kỳ thuộc địa.

sents.t: In recent years, several governments have formally requested that these artefacts be returned.
sents.vi: Những năm gần đây, nhiều chính phủ đã chính thức yêu cầu trả lại các hiện vật này.

sents.t: In 2022, Germany began transferring ownership of more than 1,000 bronze sculptures to Nigeria.
sents.vi: Năm 2022, Đức bắt đầu chuyển quyền sở hữu hơn 1.000 tác phẩm điêu khắc bằng đồng cho Nigeria.

sents.t: Some museum directors have argued that objects are better protected and more widely seen in large international collections.
sents.vi: Một số giám đốc bảo tàng cho rằng hiện vật được bảo vệ tốt hơn và được nhiều người xem hơn ở các bộ sưu tập quốc tế lớn.

sents.t: Critics reply that this argument ignores the circumstances in which the objects were acquired.
sents.vi: Những người phản đối đáp rằng lập luận này phớt lờ hoàn cảnh hiện vật đã bị thu giữ.

q.q: Germany began returning bronze sculptures to Nigeria in 2022.
All museum directors support returning colonial artefacts.
The returned sculptures are now displayed in a new museum in Lagos.

gram.title: Relative clauses with prepositions
gram.rule: the village in which … · the people to whom … · the extent to which … · the period during which … · some / many / all of which / whom
gram.note: In formal English, the preposition moves to the front of the relative clause: the village where I grew up → the village in which I grew up. After a preposition, use which for things and whom for people — never that. Quantifier + of which / whom adds information about a group: The museum has 5,000 objects, many of which were donated.

ex.t: This is the house in which my grandfather was born.
ex.vi: Đây là ngôi nhà nơi ông tôi được sinh ra.

ex.t: It is unclear the extent to which tourism protects heritage.
ex.vi: Chưa rõ du lịch bảo vệ di sản đến mức nào.

ex.t: The artisans, most of whom are over sixty, need apprentices.
ex.vi: Các nghệ nhân, phần lớn đã ngoài sáu mươi, cần người học nghề.

ex.t: The period during which the temple was built remains uncertain.
ex.vi: Thời kỳ ngôi đền được xây vẫn chưa chắc chắn.

drill.t: The village ___ which the pottery is made is small.
drill.vi: Ngôi làng nơi làm gốm khá nhỏ.

drill.t: The man to ___ I spoke was a craftsman.
drill.vi: Người đàn ông tôi nói chuyện cùng là một nghệ nhân.

drill.t: It has 200 artefacts, most of ___ are bronze.
drill.vi: Có 200 hiện vật, phần lớn bằng đồng.

drill.t: Consider the extent to ___ it has changed.
drill.vi: Hãy xem nó đã thay đổi đến mức nào.

lines.t: Is it important to preserve old buildings in cities?
lines.vi: Bảo tồn công trình cổ trong thành phố có quan trọng không?

lines.t: Generally, yes, because they’re irreplaceable — once a building is demolished, the craftsmanship and the history it represents are gone for good. But preservation shouldn’t mean freezing a city. The most successful examples I’ve seen give old buildings new uses, so they’re lived in rather than just looked at.
lines.vi: Nhìn chung là có, vì chúng không thể thay thế — một khi bị phá, tay nghề và lịch sử nó đại diện sẽ mất vĩnh viễn. Nhưng bảo tồn không nên là đóng băng thành phố. Những ví dụ thành công nhất tôi từng thấy cho công trình cũ công năng mới, để chúng được sống trong đó chứ không chỉ để ngắm.

lines.t: Does tourism help or harm traditional culture?
lines.vi: Du lịch giúp hay hại văn hoá truyền thống?

lines.t: Both. It gives communities a financial reason to keep crafts and festivals alive, which matters when young people would otherwise leave. The risk is commodification — rituals being shortened or changed to suit tourists’ schedules, until they lose the meaning they had for the community itself.
lines.vi: Cả hai. Nó cho cộng đồng lý do tài chính để duy trì nghề thủ công và lễ hội, điều quan trọng khi người trẻ có thể bỏ đi. Rủi ro là hàng hoá hoá — nghi lễ bị rút ngắn hay thay đổi cho hợp lịch trình du khách, đến khi mất đi ý nghĩa với chính cộng đồng.

lines.t: Can technology help preserve heritage?
lines.vi: Công nghệ có giúp bảo tồn di sản không?

lines.t: Enormously. Digitising manuscripts and 3D-scanning monuments means that even if the original is damaged, detailed records survive. But a recording of a song isn’t the same as people still singing it, so technology complements living traditions rather than replacing them.
lines.vi: Rất nhiều. Số hoá bản thảo và quét 3D di tích nghĩa là kể cả khi bản gốc hư hại, hồ sơ chi tiết vẫn còn. Nhưng bản ghi một bài hát không giống việc người ta vẫn hát nó, nên công nghệ bổ trợ chứ không thay thế truyền thống sống.

gram2.title: Substitution and ellipsis
gram2.rule: do so / doing so · one / ones · so / not after think, hope, expect · the former / the latter · that of / those of
gram2.note: Repeating the same words makes writing heavy. Use do so to replace a verb phrase: Many want to visit the site, but few are permitted to do so. Use one(s) for countable nouns, and that of / those of to avoid repeating a noun in comparisons: The population of Hanoi is larger than that of Hue. In speech, I think so / I hope not are natural short answers.

ex.t: Some villages have kept their crafts alive; others have failed to do so.
ex.vi: Một số làng giữ được nghề; những làng khác không làm được như vậy.

ex.t: The new museum is impressive, but I prefer the old one.
ex.vi: Bảo tàng mới ấn tượng, nhưng tôi thích bảo tàng cũ hơn.

ex.t: The festival in Hue is older than that of Hoi An.
ex.vi: Lễ hội ở Huế lâu đời hơn lễ hội ở Hội An.

ex.t: Will the tradition survive? I hope so.
ex.vi: Truyền thống có tồn tại không? Tôi hy vọng là có.

drill.t: They planned to restore it but did not ___.
drill.vi: Họ định trùng tu nhưng không làm.

drill.t: The climate of the north is colder than ___ of the south.
drill.vi: Khí hậu miền Bắc lạnh hơn khí hậu miền Nam.

drill.t: I like old houses more than modern ___.
drill.vi: Tôi thích nhà cổ hơn nhà hiện đại.

drill.t: Will it rain on the festival day? I hope ___.
drill.vi: Hôm lễ hội trời có mưa không? Tôi hy vọng là không.

cue.card: Describe a traditional skill or craft from your country.
points: what the skill or craft is
and explain why you think it should be preserved
model: I’d like to talk about Dong Ho woodblock printing, a folk art from a village of the same name in Bac Ninh province, about forty kilometres from Hanoi.

The prints are traditionally made for Tet and show simple, cheerful scenes — pigs with piglets, children with toads, a mouse wedding — each of which carries a wish for prosperity or happiness. What makes them special is the process. The paper, called “điệp”, is made from the bark of a local tree and coated with powdered seashells, which gives it a slightly sparkling surface. The colours all come from natural sources: black from burnt bamboo leaves, red from a type of gravel, yellow from flowers. Each colour is printed with a separate carved wooden block, one after another, so a single picture might require four or five blocks.

Unfortunately, it’s an endangered craft. Decades ago, almost every family in the village produced prints; now only a couple of families, most of whose members are elderly, still do so. I think it deserves to be preserved for two reasons. It’s a record of how ordinary people lived and what they hoped for, which official history rarely captures. And it’s a genuinely sustainable art form, made entirely from local, natural materials — something that seems more relevant now than ever.

write.prompt: The table shows the number of visitors (in thousands) to four heritage sites in a country, and the percentage who were international tourists, in 2010 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Site              Visitors 2010   Visitors 2024   International 2010   International 2024
Ancient citadel   850             1,900           62%                  41%
Royal tombs       400             520             70%                  68%
Hill temple       120             760             15%                  12%
Old trading port  1,100           1,350           55%                  72%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase both measures
Overview: all sites grew; hill temple fastest proportionally, citadel largest absolute; international share fell at three sites but rose at the port
Body 1: visitor numbers — compare growth rates and rankings
Body 2: international share — domestic tourism boom at citadel vs port becoming more international
model: The table compares visitor numbers at four heritage sites in a particular country in 2010 and 2024, together with the proportion of those visitors who came from abroad.

Overall, every site attracted more visitors in 2024 than in 2010, with the ancient citadel and the hill temple growing most rapidly. Meanwhile, the share of international tourists fell at three of the four sites, suggesting that much of the growth came from domestic tourism, the only exception being the old trading port.

The ancient citadel saw the largest increase in absolute terms, with visitor numbers more than doubling from 850,000 to 1.9 million, which made it the most visited site by 2024, overtaking the old trading port. The most dramatic growth in relative terms, however, was at the hill temple, where attendance rose more than sixfold, from 120,000 to 760,000. By contrast, the royal tombs and the trading port recorded more modest increases of around 30% and 23% respectively.

As for the origin of visitors, the citadel underwent the most marked shift: international tourists accounted for 62% of its visitors in 2010 but only 41% in 2024. The proportions at the royal tombs and the hill temple declined only marginally and remained very different from each other, at roughly two-thirds and one-eighth respectively. The old trading port moved in the opposite direction, with the international share rising from 55% to almost three-quarters.

units.title: Fashion & sustainable consumption
units.goal: Evaluate fast fashion and consumer responsibility, using advanced cause-and-effect language.

words.ex: Fast fashion produces cheap clothes very quickly.
words.exVi: Thời trang nhanh sản xuất quần áo rẻ rất nhanh.

words.ex: The factory produces 10,000 garments a day.
words.exVi: Nhà máy sản xuất 10.000 sản phẩm may mặc mỗi ngày.

words.ex: Textile waste is filling landfills.
words.exVi: Rác thải dệt may đang lấp đầy bãi chôn lấp.

words.ex: Clothes have become almost disposable.
words.exVi: Quần áo gần như trở thành đồ dùng rồi bỏ.

words.ex: Some brands rely on sweatshops.
words.exVi: Một số thương hiệu dựa vào xưởng bóc lột.

words.vi: tìm nguồn cung có đạo đức
words.ex: Ethical sourcing ensures fair wages.
words.exVi: Tìm nguồn cung có đạo đức đảm bảo lương công bằng.

words.ex: A circular economy keeps materials in use.
words.exVi: Kinh tế tuần hoàn giữ vật liệu được sử dụng tiếp.

words.ex: She upcycles old jeans into bags.
words.exVi: Cô ấy tái chế quần jean cũ thành túi.

words.ex: Durability matters more than price.
words.exVi: Độ bền quan trọng hơn giá.

words.ex: Synthetic clothes release microplastics when washed.
words.exVi: Quần áo tổng hợp thải vi nhựa khi giặt.

words.ex: The problem stems from overproduction.
words.exVi: Vấn đề bắt nguồn từ sản xuất quá mức.

words.ex: Cheap prices have given rise to overconsumption.
words.exVi: Giá rẻ đã làm nảy sinh tiêu dùng quá mức.

words.ex: About 10% of emissions are attributable to fashion.
words.exVi: Khoảng 10% khí thải có thể quy cho ngành thời trang.

words.ex: The factory collapse triggered global protests.
words.exVi: Vụ sập nhà máy châm ngòi biểu tình toàn cầu.

words.ex: Flash sales encourage impulse purchases.
words.exVi: Đợt giảm giá chớp nhoáng khuyến khích mua bốc đồng.

words.ex: The secondhand market is growing fast.
words.exVi: Thị trường đồ cũ đang tăng nhanh.

words.ex: Consumers demand supply chain transparency.
words.exVi: Người tiêu dùng đòi hỏi minh bạch chuỗi cung ứng.

words.ex: Buy quality, as opposed to quantity.
words.exVi: Mua chất lượng, thay vì số lượng.

words.ex: Overconsumption drains natural resources.
words.exVi: Tiêu dùng quá mức làm cạn kiệt tài nguyên.

words.ex: Toxic dyes pollute rivers near factories.
words.exVi: Thuốc nhuộm độc hại làm ô nhiễm sông gần nhà máy.

lines.t: How often do you buy new clothes?
lines.vi: Bạn mua quần áo mới thường xuyên không?

lines.t: Much less than I used to. In my early twenties I bought something almost every month, often on impulse during online sales. Now I buy a few good-quality items a year, as opposed to lots of cheap ones.
lines.vi: Ít hơn trước nhiều. Hồi đầu tuổi hai mươi, gần như tháng nào tôi cũng mua, thường là bốc đồng trong các đợt giảm giá trực tuyến. Giờ tôi mua vài món chất lượng tốt mỗi năm thay vì nhiều món rẻ.

lines.t: Do you ever buy second-hand clothes?
lines.vi: Bạn có bao giờ mua quần áo cũ không?

lines.t: Yes, especially jackets. There are some great vintage shops in Hanoi, and the quality is often better than new fast-fashion items.
lines.vi: Có, nhất là áo khoác. Ở Hà Nội có vài cửa hàng đồ cũ rất hay, và chất lượng thường tốt hơn đồ thời trang nhanh mới.

lines.t: What do you do with clothes you no longer wear?
lines.vi: Bạn làm gì với quần áo không mặc nữa?

lines.t: Usually I give them to relatives or donate them. I’ve recently learned, though, that a lot of donated clothing ends up being shipped abroad and dumped, so donation isn’t as simple a solution as I thought.
lines.vi: Thường tôi cho họ hàng hoặc quyên góp. Tuy nhiên gần đây tôi biết rằng nhiều quần áo quyên góp bị chuyển ra nước ngoài rồi vứt bỏ, nên quyên góp không phải giải pháp đơn giản như tôi nghĩ.

read.title: The true cost of cheap clothes

sents.t: Global clothing production roughly doubled between 2000 and 2015, while the average number of times a garment was worn fell by about a third.
sents.vi: Sản lượng quần áo toàn cầu tăng gần gấp đôi từ 2000 đến 2015, trong khi số lần trung bình một món đồ được mặc giảm khoảng một phần ba.

sents.t: Less than one per cent of the material used to make clothing is recycled into new clothes.
sents.vi: Chưa đến 1% vật liệu làm quần áo được tái chế thành quần áo mới.

sents.t: Much of the remainder is burned or sent to landfill, often in countries far from where it was sold.
sents.vi: Phần lớn còn lại bị đốt hoặc chôn lấp, thường ở những nước xa nơi chúng được bán.

sents.t: In Ghana, a single market receives around fifteen million used garments every week, many of which are unsellable.
sents.vi: Ở Ghana, một khu chợ duy nhất nhận khoảng mười lăm triệu món đồ cũ mỗi tuần, nhiều món không bán được.

sents.t: Campaigners argue that producers should be made responsible for what happens to their clothes after use.
sents.vi: Các nhà vận động cho rằng nhà sản xuất nên chịu trách nhiệm cho số phận quần áo của họ sau khi sử dụng.

q.q: Clothing production about doubled between 2000 and 2015.
Most clothing material is recycled into new clothes.
Ghana has banned imports of used clothing.

gram.title: Advanced cause and effect
gram.rule: stem from · arise from · be attributable to · give rise to · trigger · fuel · contribute to · exacerbate · be a by-product of
gram.note: Band 7+ writing avoids repeating “cause” and “lead to”. Notice the direction: stem from, arise from and be attributable to go from effect back to cause (The pollution stems from dyeing). Give rise to, trigger, fuel and exacerbate go from cause to effect (Low prices fuel overconsumption). Exacerbate means “make a bad situation worse”.

ex.t: Much of the pollution stems from the dyeing process.
ex.vi: Phần lớn ô nhiễm bắt nguồn từ khâu nhuộm.

ex.t: Cheap prices have given rise to a throwaway culture.
ex.vi: Giá rẻ đã làm nảy sinh văn hoá dùng rồi vứt.

ex.t: Social media fuels the demand for new outfits.
ex.vi: Mạng xã hội thổi bùng nhu cầu trang phục mới.

ex.t: Synthetic fabrics exacerbate microplastic pollution.
ex.vi: Vải tổng hợp làm trầm trọng thêm ô nhiễm vi nhựa.

drill.t: The waste problem ___ from overproduction.
drill.vi: Vấn đề rác bắt nguồn từ sản xuất quá mức.

drill.t: The disaster ___ international outrage.
drill.vi: Thảm hoạ châm ngòi cho sự phẫn nộ quốc tế.

drill.t: Low wages are partly ___ to weak unions.
drill.vi: Lương thấp một phần là do công đoàn yếu.

drill.t: Drought ___ the water shortage.
drill.vi: Hạn hán làm trầm trọng thêm tình trạng thiếu nước.

lines.t: Why do people buy so many clothes nowadays?
lines.vi: Vì sao ngày nay người ta mua nhiều quần áo thế?

lines.t: Mainly because clothes have become so cheap relative to income, and because fashion cycles have sped up dramatically — some brands release new designs every week. Social media also plays a role; people feel they can’t be photographed in the same outfit twice.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu vì quần áo trở nên quá rẻ so với thu nhập, và vì chu kỳ thời trang tăng tốc chóng mặt — một số thương hiệu ra mẫu mới mỗi tuần. Mạng xã hội cũng góp phần; người ta cảm thấy không thể bị chụp ảnh hai lần với cùng một bộ đồ.

lines.t: Should consumers or companies be responsible for the environmental impact of fashion?
lines.vi: Người tiêu dùng hay doanh nghiệp nên chịu trách nhiệm cho tác động môi trường của thời trang?

lines.t: Primarily companies, I’d argue, because they decide what materials to use and how much to produce. Consumers have limited information — it’s almost impossible to know how a T-shirt was made. Laws requiring supply chain transparency and making producers responsible for recycling would change behaviour far faster than appeals to shoppers.
lines.vi: Tôi cho rằng chủ yếu là doanh nghiệp, vì họ quyết định dùng vật liệu gì và sản xuất bao nhiêu. Người tiêu dùng có ít thông tin — gần như không thể biết một chiếc áo phông được làm thế nào. Luật yêu cầu minh bạch chuỗi cung ứng và buộc nhà sản xuất chịu trách nhiệm tái chế sẽ thay đổi hành vi nhanh hơn nhiều so với kêu gọi người mua.

lines.t: Will people buy fewer things in the future?
lines.vi: Tương lai người ta có mua ít đồ hơn không?

lines.t: Possibly in terms of new products. The secondhand and rental markets are growing quickly among young people, partly for environmental reasons and partly simply because it’s cheaper. Whether that offsets overall growth in consumption is less certain.
lines.vi: Có thể là với sản phẩm mới. Thị trường đồ cũ và cho thuê đang tăng nhanh ở người trẻ, một phần vì môi trường và một phần đơn giản vì rẻ hơn. Liệu điều đó có bù được mức tăng tiêu dùng tổng thể hay không thì kém chắc chắn hơn.

gram2.title: Contrasting alternatives
gram2.rule: as opposed to · rather than · unlike · in contrast to · instead of + -ing · whereas
gram2.note: These expressions let you compare two options precisely. As opposed to and in contrast to are followed by a noun phrase. Unlike compares two things that are similar in category: Unlike cotton, polyester does not biodegrade. Rather than and instead of can be followed by -ing: buy fewer items rather than / instead of buying many cheap ones.

ex.t: Unlike cotton, polyester is made from oil.
ex.vi: Khác với cotton, polyester được làm từ dầu mỏ.

ex.t: Repairing clothes, as opposed to replacing them, saves money.
ex.vi: Sửa quần áo, thay vì thay mới, giúp tiết kiệm tiền.

ex.t: In contrast to fast fashion, slow fashion focuses on durability.
ex.vi: Trái với thời trang nhanh, thời trang chậm chú trọng độ bền.

cue.card: Describe an item of clothing that you have kept for a long time.
points: and explain why you have kept it for so long
model: I’d like to talk about a dark green wool jacket that used to belong to my father. I’ve had it for about eight years, but it’s actually much older — he bought it in the early nineties when he worked in Russia for a couple of years.

He gave it to me when I moved to Hanoi for university, mainly because he said I’d need something warm for the northern winter and he no longer wore it. At first I thought it was rather old-fashioned, so it stayed in the wardrobe. Then a few years ago that style came back into fashion, and suddenly friends were asking where I’d bought it.

These days I wear it most weeks between December and February. I’ve kept it for several reasons. Practically, it’s far better made than anything I could buy at a similar price now — the stitching is still perfect after thirty years, which is quite a contrast to some fast-fashion shirts I’ve owned that lost their shape after a few washes. But the main reason is sentimental. It reminds me of my father’s stories about that period of his life, and in a sense it connects his youth with mine. It’s also made me think about how much of our clothing is designed to be disposable, as opposed to something you might pass on.

write.prompt: The fashion industry has become one of the world’s major polluters. What are the causes of this, and what measures could be taken to reduce the environmental impact of clothing?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + outline causes (fast production model, synthetic materials, low recycling) and solutions (regulation, producer responsibility, consumer shift)
Body 1: causes — overproduction and short cycles; synthetic fibres and dyes; disposal problem; specific data
Body 2: solutions — extended producer responsibility; standards and transparency laws; durable design and repair; secondhand
Conclusion: systemic causes need systemic solutions
model: Clothing production has expanded dramatically in recent decades, and the industry is now responsible for a significant share of global pollution. This problem stems mainly from a business model based on rapid, high-volume production of cheap garments, combined with materials that are difficult to recycle. Addressing it will require regulation of producers as well as changes in consumer behaviour.

The principal cause is the rise of fast fashion. Many brands now release new collections every few weeks, which has given rise to a culture in which clothes are bought cheaply, worn a handful of times and discarded. Global production roughly doubled in the first fifteen years of this century, while the average number of times each garment was worn fell sharply. The materials themselves exacerbate the problem: polyester and other synthetic fibres are derived from oil and release microplastics when washed, while dyeing processes in some producing countries discharge toxic chemicals into rivers. Finally, less than one per cent of clothing material is recycled into new garments, so most ends up in landfill or is incinerated.

Several measures could reduce this impact. Firstly, governments could introduce extended producer responsibility schemes, whereby brands pay for the collection and recycling of the clothes they sell. This would give companies a financial incentive to design durable, recyclable products. Secondly, laws requiring supply chain transparency and enforcing environmental standards in factories would make it harder for firms to outsource pollution to countries with weak regulation. Consumers also have a role, for instance by buying fewer but better-quality items, repairing clothes and using secondhand or rental services, but such changes are more likely to spread if they are supported by pricing and policy rather than left to individual conscience.

In conclusion, the environmental damage caused by fashion is largely attributable to a system that rewards overproduction and disposability. Since the causes are structural, the most effective solutions are likely to be regulatory, making producers responsible for the full life cycle of their products, while encouraging consumers to value durability over novelty.

lines.t: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
lines.vi: Bạn thích làm việc một mình hay theo nhóm?

lines.t: It depends on the task. For detailed calculations, alone, because I need to concentrate. But for solving complex problems, a team is far better — someone always spots what I’ve missed.
lines.vi: Tuỳ việc. Với tính toán chi tiết thì một mình, vì tôi cần tập trung. Nhưng với vấn đề phức tạp thì làm nhóm tốt hơn nhiều — luôn có người phát hiện điều tôi bỏ sót.

lines.t: Have you ever been a leader?
lines.vi: Bạn đã bao giờ làm trưởng nhóm chưa?

lines.t: In a small way. I led a team of four engineers on a project last year. The hardest part was learning to delegate rather than trying to check every single detail myself.
lines.vi: Ở quy mô nhỏ. Năm ngoái tôi dẫn dắt nhóm bốn kỹ sư trong một dự án. Phần khó nhất là học cách giao việc thay vì tự kiểm tra từng chi tiết.

lines.t: What makes a good manager?

lines.t: For me, someone approachable who gives clear goals and then trusts you to reach them. The worst managers I’ve had were the ones who micromanaged everything.
lines.vi: Với tôi là người dễ gần, đưa ra mục tiêu rõ ràng rồi tin tưởng bạn đạt được. Những người quản lý tệ nhất tôi từng gặp là những người can thiệp vào mọi thứ.

sents.t: A large study by a technology company examined more than 180 of its internal teams to find out why some performed better than others.
sents.vi: Một nghiên cứu lớn của một công ty công nghệ khảo sát hơn 180 nhóm nội bộ để tìm hiểu vì sao một số nhóm làm việc tốt hơn.

sents.t: Researchers expected that the best teams would contain the most talented or experienced individuals.
sents.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu từng nghĩ các nhóm tốt nhất sẽ gồm những cá nhân tài năng hoặc giàu kinh nghiệm nhất.

sents.t: Instead, the most important factor was psychological safety: whether members felt able to take risks and admit mistakes without being embarrassed.
sents.vi: Thay vào đó, yếu tố quan trọng nhất là an toàn tâm lý: các thành viên có cảm thấy dám chấp nhận rủi ro và thừa nhận lỗi mà không bị xấu hổ hay không.

sents.t: Teams in which everyone spoke roughly equally also tended to perform better.
sents.vi: Các nhóm mà mọi người phát biểu tương đối ngang nhau cũng có xu hướng làm việc tốt hơn.

sents.t: The findings suggest that a leader’s main role may be to create the right conditions rather than to have all the answers.
sents.vi: Kết quả cho thấy vai trò chính của người lãnh đạo có thể là tạo điều kiện phù hợp hơn là có mọi câu trả lời.

q.q: The researchers’ original expectation was confirmed by the study.
Psychological safety was the most important factor in team performance.
The best teams had the smallest number of members.

gram.title: Verbs whose meaning changes with -ing or to
gram.rule: stop / remember / forget / try / regret / go on / mean + -ing vs + to
gram.note: With these verbs, the choice between -ing and to-infinitive changes the meaning. Remember doing = remember a past action; remember to do = not forget a duty. Stop doing = quit; stop to do = pause in order to do. Try doing = experiment; try to do = make an effort. Regret to inform is formal bad news. Go on to do = do something next.

lines.t: Are leaders born or made?
lines.vi: Lãnh đạo là bẩm sinh hay được đào tạo?

lines.t: Mostly made, I think. Some traits help — confidence, perhaps charisma — but the skills that matter most, like listening, giving constructive feedback and making decisions with incomplete information, can be learned. Some of the most effective leaders I’ve seen were quite introverted.
lines.vi: Chủ yếu là được rèn luyện, tôi nghĩ vậy. Một số tố chất có ích — sự tự tin, có lẽ cả sức hút — nhưng những kỹ năng quan trọng nhất như lắng nghe, góp ý xây dựng và ra quyết định khi thông tin chưa đầy đủ đều học được. Một số nhà lãnh đạo hiệu quả nhất tôi từng thấy khá hướng nội.

lines.t: Is a strict hierarchy good for a company?
lines.vi: Cấp bậc nghiêm ngặt có tốt cho công ty không?

lines.t: In some situations — the military, or an emergency in a hospital — clear lines of authority save lives. But in creative or technical work, a rigid hierarchy tends to discourage junior staff from speaking up, and the people closest to a problem often have the best ideas.
lines.vi: Trong một số tình huống — quân đội, hay cấp cứu ở bệnh viện — tuyến quyền hạn rõ ràng cứu người. Nhưng trong công việc sáng tạo hay kỹ thuật, cấp bậc cứng nhắc thường khiến nhân viên cấp dưới ngại lên tiếng, trong khi người gần vấn đề nhất thường có ý tưởng tốt nhất.

lines.t: Should political leaders have a background in business?
lines.vi: Lãnh đạo chính trị có nên có nền tảng kinh doanh?

lines.t: It can help with managing budgets, but governing isn’t the same as running a company. A business can choose its customers; a government has to serve everyone, including people who will never be profitable. So I’d value integrity and the ability to build consensus more than business experience.
lines.vi: Nó có thể giúp quản lý ngân sách, nhưng điều hành đất nước không giống điều hành công ty. Doanh nghiệp có thể chọn khách hàng; chính phủ phải phục vụ tất cả, kể cả những người không bao giờ sinh lời. Nên tôi coi trọng sự chính trực và khả năng xây dựng đồng thuận hơn kinh nghiệm kinh doanh.

cue.card: Describe a person you have worked or studied with who was a good leader.
points: what they did as a leader
and explain why you think they were a good leader
model: I’d like to talk about Ms Thu, who was the project director on the first major building I worked on after graduating — a fifteen-storey office block in Da Nang.

About halfway through the project, we discovered that some of the foundation tests had been done incorrectly by a subcontractor, which meant a three-week delay and a serious risk of going over budget. I remember thinking the whole team would be blamed, and morale dropped sharply.

What she did impressed me enormously. First, she stayed remarkably level-headed — she called a meeting the same afternoon and simply laid out the facts without blaming anyone. Then she asked each of us, including the most junior engineers like me, for ideas on how to recover time, and two of the solutions we eventually used came from people who would never normally have spoken in that kind of meeting. Finally, she went to the client herself and took full accountability, rather than sending someone else. I think she was a good leader because she created what researchers call psychological safety: people weren’t afraid to admit mistakes or suggest ideas. I remember being surprised that a senior person would ask my opinion, and I’ve tried to lead my own small team the same way since then.

write.prompt: The pie charts show the results of a survey of employees in one company about their satisfaction with management in 2015 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
write.data:
Rating               2015    2025
Very satisfied        12%     31%
Satisfied             28%     39%
Neutral               25%     15%
Dissatisfied          23%     10%
Very dissatisfied     12%      5%
plan: Introduction: paraphrase (survey of employees, satisfaction with management)
Overview: marked improvement; satisfied groups rose from 40% to 70%; dissatisfied halved+
Body 1: positive ratings — very satisfied nearly tripled; satisfied rose
Body 2: neutral and negative — all declined; combine to show the reversal
model: The two pie charts compare how satisfied employees in a particular company were with its management in 2015 and 2025.

Overall, attitudes towards management improved considerably over the decade. While only two-fifths of staff expressed satisfaction in 2015, this proportion had risen to seven in ten by 2025, and the share of dissatisfied employees fell sharply.

The most striking change was in the “very satisfied” category, which accounted for just 12% of responses in 2015 but almost tripled to 31% ten years later. The proportion who were satisfied also grew, from 28% to 39%, so that together these two groups rose from 40% to 70% of the workforce.

Meanwhile, every other category declined. The share of neutral responses dropped from a quarter to 15%. Dissatisfaction decreased even more markedly: the percentage of employees who were dissatisfied more than halved, from 23% to 10%, and the proportion who were very dissatisfied fell from 12% to only 5%. As a result, negative ratings, which had made up over a third of responses in 2015, accounted for just 15% in 2025.

lines.t: Have you ever done any volunteer work?
lines.vi: Bạn đã bao giờ làm tình nguyện chưa?

lines.t: Yes, during university I spent two summers teaching English to children in a mountainous district of Lao Cai. It was exhausting but probably the most meaningful thing I did as a student.
lines.vi: Có, thời đại học tôi dành hai mùa hè dạy tiếng Anh cho trẻ em ở một huyện miền núi Lào Cai. Rất mệt nhưng có lẽ là điều ý nghĩa nhất tôi làm khi còn là sinh viên.

lines.t: Do people in your country often help their neighbours?
lines.vi: Người dân nước bạn có hay giúp hàng xóm không?

lines.t: In villages, definitely — there’s a strong sense of community. In city apartment buildings it’s less common, though during the floods a few years ago, our building organised itself remarkably quickly.
lines.vi: Ở làng quê thì chắc chắn — có ý thức cộng đồng mạnh. Ở chung cư thành phố thì ít hơn, dù trong đợt lũ vài năm trước, toà nhà chúng tôi tự tổ chức nhanh đáng kinh ngạc.

sents.t: A long-term study of older adults found that those who volunteered regularly reported higher life satisfaction and lower rates of depression.
sents.vi: Một nghiên cứu dài hạn về người cao tuổi cho thấy những người tình nguyện thường xuyên báo cáo mức hài lòng cuộc sống cao hơn và tỉ lệ trầm cảm thấp hơn.

sents.t: They also appeared to live slightly longer, even after differences in income and health were taken into account.
sents.vi: Họ cũng có vẻ sống lâu hơn một chút, ngay cả sau khi đã tính đến khác biệt về thu nhập và sức khoẻ.

sents.t: However, the benefits were only found among people whose main motivation was helping others.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, lợi ích chỉ thấy ở những người có động lực chính là giúp đỡ người khác.

sents.t: Those who volunteered mainly to improve their own situation showed no difference compared with non-volunteers.
sents.vi: Những người tình nguyện chủ yếu để cải thiện tình cảnh bản thân không có khác biệt so với người không tình nguyện.

sents.t: The researchers caution that the study shows a correlation and cannot prove that volunteering itself caused the improvements.
sents.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu lưu ý nghiên cứu chỉ cho thấy tương quan và không thể chứng minh chính việc tình nguyện gây ra sự cải thiện.

q.q: The health benefits were found among all volunteers, whatever their motivation.
The study cannot prove that volunteering caused the benefits.
Most of the volunteers in the study worked in hospitals.

gram.title: Advanced passive forms
gram.rule: modal + be + past participle · needs + to be + past participle · passive infinitive (to be done) · passive gerund (being done) · perfect passive (having been done) · get + past participle
gram.note: Beyond basic tenses, the passive appears with infinitives and gerunds. Use the passive gerund after verbs and prepositions: Nobody likes being told what to do. Use the perfect passive participle for an earlier completed action: Having been trained, the volunteers were sent to the villages. Get-passives are informal and often describe something unexpected: He got injured.

ex.t: More needs to be done to support young carers.
ex.vi: Cần làm nhiều hơn để hỗ trợ người chăm sóc trẻ tuổi.

ex.t: Many volunteers dislike being treated as free labour.
ex.vi: Nhiều tình nguyện viên không thích bị đối xử như lao động miễn phí.

ex.t: Having been trained, the volunteers were sent to the shelters.
ex.vi: Sau khi được đào tạo, tình nguyện viên được cử đến các điểm trú ẩn.

ex.t: The scheme is expected to be extended next year.
ex.vi: Chương trình dự kiến sẽ được mở rộng năm sau.

drill.vi: Mái nhà cần được sửa trước mùa mưa.

drill.t: She hates ___ in front of others.
drill.vi: Cô ấy ghét bị chỉ trích trước mặt người khác.

lines.t: Should volunteering be compulsory for students?
lines.vi: Có nên bắt buộc học sinh làm tình nguyện?

lines.t: I’m in two minds. Compulsory schemes introduce young people to causes they might never have discovered, and some go on to volunteer for life. But if it becomes just another box to tick, it can feel tokenistic, and organisations end up with unmotivated helpers. On balance, I’d make it available and well-supported rather than compulsory.
lines.vi: Tôi phân vân. Chương trình bắt buộc giới thiệu cho người trẻ những mục đích họ có thể không bao giờ tự khám phá, và một số người sau đó tình nguyện suốt đời. Nhưng nếu nó chỉ là một ô cần đánh dấu, nó có thể mang tính hình thức, và các tổ chức nhận về những người giúp thiếu động lực. Nhìn chung, tôi sẽ tạo cơ hội và hỗ trợ tốt hơn là bắt buộc.

lines.t: Why are some young people uninterested in politics?
lines.vi: Vì sao một số người trẻ không quan tâm chính trị?

lines.t: I’m not sure it’s really apathy. Many young people are very engaged with specific issues — climate, animal welfare — and they’ll sign petitions or join campaigns. What they’re less interested in is traditional party politics, partly because they feel it doesn’t represent them.
lines.vi: Tôi không chắc đó thực sự là thờ ơ. Nhiều người trẻ rất quan tâm đến những vấn đề cụ thể — khí hậu, phúc lợi động vật — và họ sẽ ký kiến nghị hay tham gia chiến dịch. Điều họ ít quan tâm là chính trị đảng phái truyền thống, một phần vì họ cảm thấy nó không đại diện cho họ.

lines.t: Can volunteers replace paid professionals?
lines.vi: Tình nguyện viên có thể thay thế người làm chuyên nghiệp được trả lương không?

lines.t: They shouldn’t. Volunteers can add a great deal — time, local knowledge, human contact — but services like nursing or disaster relief need trained, accountable staff. Relying on goodwill is also unreliable; people’s availability changes.
lines.vi: Không nên. Tình nguyện viên có thể đóng góp rất nhiều — thời gian, hiểu biết địa phương, sự gần gũi — nhưng các dịch vụ như điều dưỡng hay cứu trợ thảm hoạ cần nhân viên được đào tạo và chịu trách nhiệm. Dựa vào thiện chí cũng không ổn định; thời gian rảnh của người ta thay đổi.

gram2.title: Synthesising and concluding
gram2.rule: All things considered, … · On balance, … · Ultimately, … · Taking everything into account, … · The key issue is not X but Y · It follows that …
gram2.note: A strong conclusion does more than repeat the introduction: it weighs the arguments and shows which matters more. On balance and all things considered signal that you have compared both sides. The key issue is not … but … reframes the question at a higher level, which examiners reward. Avoid introducing new arguments in the conclusion.

ex.t: All things considered, the benefits clearly outweigh the costs.
ex.vi: Xét mọi mặt, lợi ích rõ ràng lớn hơn chi phí.

ex.t: On balance, voluntary schemes work better than compulsory ones.
ex.vi: Nhìn chung, chương trình tự nguyện hiệu quả hơn bắt buộc.

ex.t: The key issue is not whether people volunteer but how they are supported.
ex.vi: Vấn đề then chốt không phải là có tình nguyện hay không mà là được hỗ trợ ra sao.

ex.t: Ultimately, a healthy society depends on active citizens.
ex.vi: Suy cho cùng, một xã hội lành mạnh dựa vào công dân tích cực.

drill.t: ___ balance, I support the idea.
drill.vi: Nhìn chung, tôi ủng hộ ý tưởng.

drill.t: All things ___, it was a success.
drill.vi: Xét mọi mặt, đó là một thành công.

drill.t: The key issue is not cost ___ quality.
drill.vi: Vấn đề then chốt không phải chi phí mà là chất lượng.

drill.t: Taking everything into ___, the plan is sound.
drill.vi: Xét tổng thể, kế hoạch hợp lý.

cue.card: Describe a time when you helped someone in your community.
points: and explain how you felt about helping
model: I’d like to describe something that happened during the floods in central Vietnam in 2020, when I was working in Hue for a few months on a construction project.

The rain went on for almost two weeks, and the area around the old citadel flooded badly. An elderly couple who lived on the ground floor of the house next to my rented room couldn’t leave — the husband had difficulty walking, and their children lived in Ho Chi Minh City. On the third morning the water was up to my knees inside their house, and their electricity had been cut off.

Together with two colleagues, I helped them move their most important belongings — family photographs, the ancestral altar, their documents — up to the second floor of a neighbour’s house, and for about a week we brought them meals and drinking water, which had been delivered to our site by the company. It wasn’t heroic; it was just a matter of being physically close and able to help. How did I feel? Honestly, more uncomfortable than proud, because it made me realise how vulnerable older people living alone are when public services are overwhelmed. All things considered, it was one of the experiences that made me think seriously about volunteering in a more organised way, and it’s why I’d now like to use my engineering skills to help design flood-resilient housing.

write.prompt: Some people think that all young people should be required to do unpaid work in their communities, for example helping the elderly or protecting the environment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + position (disagree with compulsion; support strongly encouraged, flexible, recognised schemes)
Body 1: arguments for compulsion — civic awareness, social cohesion, practical benefits; acknowledge fully
Body 2: arguments against — undermines motivation, tokenism, burden on poor students, displaces paid jobs; evidence on motivation
Conclusion: synthesise — the key issue is engagement, not attendance
model: It has been suggested that every young person should be obliged to carry out unpaid work for their community, such as caring for older people or taking part in environmental projects. While I fully agree that young people benefit from such experiences, I disagree that participation should be compulsory, because enforced volunteering tends to undermine the very motivation that makes it valuable.

The case for a requirement is not without merit. Community work exposes young people to sections of society they might otherwise never encounter, which can build empathy and a sense of civic duty. It can also strengthen social cohesion, particularly in ageing societies where isolated elderly people would benefit from regular contact with younger generations. In addition, young people often gain practical skills, from teamwork to problem-solving, that make them more employable. Some schools that have introduced service requirements report that a proportion of students continue volunteering long after they are obliged to.

However, making such work mandatory raises significant problems. Research on volunteering suggests that its benefits, both for the volunteer and for the people helped, depend heavily on genuine motivation; when participation is enforced, it risks becoming a box-ticking exercise in which young people simply attend without engaging. A compulsory scheme would also place a disproportionate burden on students from low-income families, many of whom already work part-time to support themselves or their relatives. Moreover, if large numbers of unpaid young people are deployed in care or environmental work, there is a danger that they will be used to replace paid professionals, reducing both the quality of services and the number of jobs available.

All things considered, I believe the key issue is not whether young people are made to do community work but whether they are given real opportunities and reasons to do so. On balance, governments and schools should encourage participation through flexible programmes, academic credit and recognition by employers, rather than imposing a requirement that may produce attendance without commitment.

levels.name: Band 7.5→8+
levels.title: Expert: exam mastery and subtle argument
levels.desc: Happiness, privacy, free speech, longevity, food, water, tradition, sport, research and animal ethics — abstract questions where the top bands depend on precision, flexibility and error-free control.
goals: Produce essays where every paragraph has one clear, fully extended and well-supported idea
Use less common vocabulary naturally and with awareness of style and collocation
Write long, varied sentences that are almost entirely error-free (including articles and agreement)
Paraphrase confidently and answer Part 3 questions with abstract reasoning and qualification
Finish every test section on time, with 3–5 minutes for checking
extra: Two full mock tests a week under strict timing; analyse every error by category
Read academic journals or quality long-form journalism daily for 30 minutes
Weekly one-to-one Speaking mock with an experienced IELTS teacher
Keep a personal error log and rewrite one old essay a week without those errors

units.title: Happiness & well-being
units.goal: Discuss what makes people happy and whether it can be measured, using complex noun groups and stance adverbs.

words.vi: hạnh phúc viên mãn (sống có ý nghĩa)
words.ex: Aristotle described eudaimonia as living well, not just feeling good.
words.exVi: Aristotle mô tả eudaimonia là sống tốt, không chỉ cảm thấy vui.

words.ex: Contentment is quieter than excitement.
words.exVi: Sự mãn nguyện lặng lẽ hơn sự phấn khích.

words.ex: Many find fulfilment in meaningful work.
words.exVi: Nhiều người tìm thấy sự viên mãn trong công việc ý nghĩa.

words.ex: Materialism is linked to lower life satisfaction.
words.exVi: Chủ nghĩa vật chất liên quan đến mức hài lòng cuộc sống thấp hơn.

words.vi: thích nghi khoái lạc (nhanh quen với điều tốt)
words.ex: Hedonic adaptation explains why a pay rise soon stops feeling special.
words.exVi: Thích nghi khoái lạc giải thích vì sao tăng lương nhanh chóng hết cảm giác đặc biệt.

words.ex: Happiness is partly subjective.
words.exVi: Hạnh phúc một phần mang tính chủ quan.

words.ex: It is hard to quantify happiness.
words.exVi: Rất khó định lượng hạnh phúc.

words.ex: GDP measures output, not well-being.
words.exVi: GDP đo sản lượng, không phải hạnh phúc.

words.vi: mức hài lòng với cuộc sống
words.ex: Life satisfaction is highest in Nordic countries.
words.exVi: Mức hài lòng với cuộc sống cao nhất ở các nước Bắc Âu.

words.ex: Income shows diminishing returns for happiness.
words.exVi: Thu nhập có lợi ích giảm dần đối với hạnh phúc.

words.ex: A sense of purpose protects mental health.
words.exVi: Ý thức về mục đích sống bảo vệ sức khoẻ tinh thần.

words.vi: bề ngoài thì, có vẻ như
words.ex: The app is ostensibly free.
words.exVi: Ứng dụng bề ngoài là miễn phí.

words.vi: có thể hình dung được, có khả năng
words.ex: Money could conceivably buy some happiness.
words.exVi: Tiền có khả năng mua được một phần hạnh phúc.

words.ex: Relationships are undeniably central to happiness.
words.exVi: Không thể phủ nhận các mối quan hệ là trung tâm của hạnh phúc.

words.ex: The pleasure of shopping is transient.
words.exVi: Niềm vui mua sắm chỉ thoáng qua.

words.ex: Social media intensifies social comparison.
words.exVi: Mạng xã hội làm tăng sự so sánh xã hội.

words.ex: Resilient people recover quickly from setbacks.
words.exVi: Người kiên cường hồi phục nhanh sau thất bại.

words.ex: Mindfulness can reduce stress.
words.exVi: Chánh niệm có thể giảm căng thẳng.

words.ex: The pursuit of happiness can make people anxious.
words.exVi: Việc theo đuổi hạnh phúc có thể khiến người ta lo âu.

words.ex: Intrinsic motivation lasts longer than rewards.
words.exVi: Động lực nội tại bền hơn phần thưởng.

lines.t: What makes you happy?
lines.vi: Điều gì khiến bạn hạnh phúc?

lines.t: Mostly small, ordinary things — a long dinner with friends, finishing a difficult piece of work, cycling along the river early on a Sunday. The things I once assumed would make me happy, like a bigger apartment, turned out to matter far less.
lines.vi: Phần lớn là những điều nhỏ bé, bình thường — bữa tối dài với bạn bè, hoàn thành một việc khó, đạp xe dọc sông sáng sớm Chủ nhật. Những thứ tôi từng nghĩ sẽ khiến mình hạnh phúc, như căn hộ lớn hơn, hoá ra lại ít quan trọng hơn nhiều.

lines.t: Were you happier as a child?
lines.vi: Hồi nhỏ bạn có hạnh phúc hơn không?

lines.t: In a simpler way, perhaps. Children live much more in the present, whereas adults spend a lot of time worrying about the future. But I find my happiness now more meaningful, because it comes partly from things I’ve chosen and worked for.
lines.vi: Theo cách đơn giản hơn, có lẽ vậy. Trẻ em sống trong hiện tại nhiều hơn, còn người lớn dành nhiều thời gian lo lắng về tương lai. Nhưng tôi thấy hạnh phúc của mình bây giờ ý nghĩa hơn, vì một phần đến từ những điều mình đã chọn và nỗ lực vì nó.

lines.t: Do you think people in your country are happy?
lines.vi: Bạn có nghĩ người dân nước bạn hạnh phúc không?

lines.t: Surveys suggest moderately so, and I’d say people are remarkably resilient. Family ties are strong, which undeniably helps, but work pressure and social comparison have increased a lot, especially among young urban people.
lines.vi: Khảo sát cho thấy ở mức khá, và tôi cho rằng người dân kiên cường đáng kể. Gắn kết gia đình bền chặt, điều không thể phủ nhận là có ích, nhưng áp lực công việc và so sánh xã hội đã tăng nhiều, nhất là ở người trẻ thành thị.

sents.t: A widely cited 2010 study concluded that emotional well-being stopped rising once annual income reached about 75,000 dollars.
sents.vi: Một nghiên cứu năm 2010 được dẫn nhiều kết luận rằng hạnh phúc cảm xúc ngừng tăng khi thu nhập năm đạt khoảng 75.000 đô la.

sents.t: A larger study published in 2021, however, found that well-being continued to increase with income well beyond that level.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, một nghiên cứu lớn hơn công bố năm 2021 cho thấy hạnh phúc tiếp tục tăng theo thu nhập vượt xa mức đó.

sents.t: In 2023, researchers from both teams collaborated and concluded that the plateau applies mainly to the least happy fifth of people.
sents.vi: Năm 2023, các nhà nghiên cứu của cả hai nhóm hợp tác và kết luận rằng hiện tượng chững lại chủ yếu đúng với một phần năm người kém hạnh phúc nhất.

sents.t: For this group, problems such as illness or grief appear to limit what extra income can achieve.
sents.vi: Với nhóm này, những vấn đề như bệnh tật hay mất mát dường như giới hạn những gì thu nhập thêm có thể đạt được.

sents.t: For most people, though, each doubling of income is associated with a similar, modest increase in well-being.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên với phần lớn mọi người, mỗi lần thu nhập tăng gấp đôi đi kèm mức tăng hạnh phúc tương tự và khiêm tốn.

q.q: The 2021 study supported the idea of a fixed income limit for happiness.
Researchers from the two original teams later worked together.
The 2023 study was conducted entirely in Europe.

gram.title: Complex noun groups
gram.rule: pre-modification (a widely cited study) · post-modification with prepositions (the pursuit of happiness), participles (people living alone), relative and to-clauses (the ability to adapt)
gram.note: Band 8–9 writing packs information into noun groups instead of chains of short clauses. Build them by adding adjectives and adverbs before the noun and phrases after it: the growing body of evidence linking social media use to anxiety. Keep the head noun clear so the verb agrees with it: The number of studies examining this effect HAS increased.

ex.t: A growing body of research links loneliness to poor health.
ex.vi: Ngày càng nhiều nghiên cứu liên hệ cô đơn với sức khoẻ kém.

ex.t: The pursuit of material wealth rarely brings lasting satisfaction.
ex.vi: Việc theo đuổi của cải vật chất hiếm khi mang lại sự hài lòng lâu dài.

ex.t: People living in close-knit communities report higher well-being.
ex.vi: Những người sống trong cộng đồng gắn bó báo cáo mức hạnh phúc cao hơn.

ex.t: The ability to adapt to change is crucial for resilience.
ex.vi: Khả năng thích nghi với thay đổi là then chốt cho sức bật.

drill.t: The number of people reporting stress ___ risen.
drill.vi: Số người báo cáo bị căng thẳng đã tăng.

drill.t: A ___ study suggests the opposite.
drill.vi: Một nghiên cứu mới công bố gợi ý điều ngược lại.

drill.t: Workers ___ long hours sleep less.
drill.vi: Người lao động làm nhiều giờ ngủ ít hơn.

drill.t: The decision ___ the tax was controversial.
drill.vi: Quyết định tăng thuế gây tranh cãi.

lines.t: Should governments try to increase people’s happiness?
lines.vi: Chính phủ có nên cố gắng tăng hạnh phúc của người dân không?

lines.t: Not directly, I’d argue — a government telling citizens how to be happy sounds rather sinister. But it can address the conditions that undermine well-being: insecure jobs, loneliness, poor mental health services, long commutes. Ostensibly economic policies, like housing, often have the biggest effect on how people feel.
lines.vi: Tôi cho là không nên trực tiếp — chính phủ bảo công dân cách để hạnh phúc nghe khá đáng sợ. Nhưng họ có thể giải quyết những điều kiện làm suy giảm hạnh phúc: việc làm bấp bênh, cô đơn, dịch vụ sức khoẻ tinh thần kém, đi lại xa. Những chính sách bề ngoài là kinh tế như nhà ở thường tác động lớn nhất đến cảm nhận của người dân.

lines.t: Is GDP a good measure of a country’s success?
lines.vi: GDP có phải thước đo tốt cho thành công của một quốc gia?

lines.t: It’s a good measure of economic activity, but a poor measure of success. GDP rises after a natural disaster because of rebuilding, and it counts pollution clean-up as growth. Several countries now publish well-being indicators alongside GDP, which seems a sensible complement rather than a replacement.
lines.vi: Đó là thước đo tốt cho hoạt động kinh tế, nhưng là thước đo kém cho thành công. GDP tăng sau thiên tai vì tái thiết, và nó tính việc dọn dẹp ô nhiễm là tăng trưởng. Một số nước giờ công bố chỉ số hạnh phúc song song với GDP, có vẻ là sự bổ sung hợp lý chứ không phải thay thế.

lines.t: Why might richer societies not be happier?
lines.vi: Vì sao xã hội giàu hơn có thể không hạnh phúc hơn?

lines.t: Partly hedonic adaptation — we quickly get used to higher living standards — and partly social comparison: if everyone’s income rises, nobody feels relatively better off. Rich societies can also lose things that are hard to price, like time with family or a sense of community.
lines.vi: Một phần là do thích nghi khoái lạc — ta nhanh chóng quen với mức sống cao hơn — và một phần do so sánh xã hội: nếu thu nhập của ai cũng tăng, không ai cảm thấy khá hơn tương đối. Xã hội giàu cũng có thể đánh mất những thứ khó định giá, như thời gian bên gia đình hay ý thức cộng đồng.

gram2.title: Stance adverbs
gram2.rule: admittedly · arguably · conceivably · ostensibly · undeniably · understandably · paradoxically · predictably
gram2.note: Stance adverbs show your attitude to a statement in a single word, which is elegant and efficient. Each has a precise meaning: ostensibly = it appears so, but may not be true; conceivably = it is possible to imagine; paradoxically = surprisingly contradictory. Place them at the start of a sentence or before the main verb.

ex.t: Paradoxically, the more choices people have, the less satisfied they feel.
ex.vi: Nghịch lý thay, người ta càng có nhiều lựa chọn càng kém hài lòng.

ex.t: The policy was ostensibly designed to help families.

cue.card: Describe a time when you felt very satisfied with something you achieved.
points: what you had to do to achieve it
and explain why it gave you so much satisfaction
model: The achievement I’d like to describe is completing my first half-marathon, which I ran in Hanoi about two years ago — not quickly, I should say, but without stopping.

What makes it meaningful is where I started from. A year earlier, I was someone who got out of breath climbing the stairs to my office on the fourth floor. After a health check flagged high blood pressure, I decided I needed a concrete goal rather than vague intentions, so I signed up for the race nine months in advance, which made it embarrassing to back out. I followed a beginner’s programme, starting with alternating one minute of jogging and one of walking, and gradually built up to three runs a week. There were plenty of setbacks — a knee injury in the fourth month set me back several weeks — and more than once I seriously considered giving up.

The satisfaction came less from crossing the finish line itself, which was mostly painful, than from what it represented. It was undeniably the first time as an adult that I’d set myself a long-term goal with no external reward — no grade, no salary — and achieved it through steady, unglamorous effort. Paradoxically, the most valuable thing I gained wasn’t fitness but a kind of evidence about myself: that I can change habits I’d assumed were fixed. That has made me more willing to take on other difficult things since.

write.prompt: Some people believe that economic growth is the best way for a country to improve the happiness of its citizens. Others argue that other factors are more important. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: precise paraphrase + nuanced thesis (growth is necessary up to a point but insufficient; distribution and non-material factors dominate in middle/high-income countries)
Body 1: case for growth — poverty, health, security; evidence from income–well-being studies
Body 2: case for other factors — diminishing returns, relative income, relationships, trust, health systems; Nordic/Costa Rica example
Conclusion: synthesis — growth as a means, not an end
model: Whether prosperity is the most reliable route to a happier population is a question that divides economists and policymakers. While some maintain that economic growth remains the most effective means of raising well-being, others contend that factors such as social relationships, health and public trust matter more. In my view, growth is indispensable for poorer nations, but beyond a certain level of income, how wealth is distributed and how people live become considerably more important than further expansion.

The argument for prioritising growth is strongest where material deprivation is widespread. Rising national income allows governments to fund clean water, healthcare and education, and it enables households to escape the chronic insecurity that poverty brings. Large-scale studies consistently find that, within and across countries, richer people report higher life satisfaction on average, and recent research suggests that this association persists even at relatively high incomes. From this perspective, dismissing growth as irrelevant to happiness would be both inaccurate and, for the world’s poorest, irresponsible.

Nevertheless, the relationship between income and well-being is far from straightforward. Each additional dollar tends to produce a smaller gain in happiness than the last, and because people judge their circumstances partly by comparison with others, a general rise in incomes can leave individuals feeling no better off. Moreover, several of the factors most strongly linked to life satisfaction — secure employment, close relationships, good physical and mental health, and trust in public institutions — are only loosely connected to GDP. This helps to explain why countries such as Costa Rica report levels of well-being comparable to those of far wealthier nations, while some rapidly growing economies have seen little improvement in how their citizens feel.

In conclusion, economic growth is a necessary foundation for happiness, particularly in low-income countries, but it is not sufficient on its own. Governments of middle- and high-income countries should therefore treat growth as a means rather than an end, and judge their success by broader measures that capture health, social connection and security, alongside the conventional indicators of prosperity.

units.title: Surveillance & privacy
units.goal: Debate privacy, security and data, using the formal subjunctive and inverted conditionals.

lines.t: Do you worry about your privacy online?
lines.vi: Bạn có lo về quyền riêng tư trên mạng không?

lines.t: More than I used to. I’ve started reading which permissions apps request, and I was genuinely surprised how many want my location or contacts for no obvious reason.
lines.vi: Nhiều hơn trước. Tôi bắt đầu đọc xem ứng dụng xin những quyền gì, và thực sự ngạc nhiên vì nhiều ứng dụng muốn vị trí hay danh bạ của tôi mà không có lý do rõ ràng.

lines.t: Do you share much on social media?
lines.vi: Bạn có chia sẻ nhiều trên mạng xã hội không?

lines.t: Very little now. I post occasionally, but never anything that reveals where I live or my daily routine. A friend had her account hacked a few years ago and it made me much more cautious.
lines.vi: Giờ rất ít. Thỉnh thoảng tôi đăng bài, nhưng không bao giờ đăng gì tiết lộ nơi ở hay lịch sinh hoạt. Một người bạn bị hack tài khoản vài năm trước và điều đó khiến tôi thận trọng hơn nhiều.

lines.t: Is privacy more important to older or younger people?
lines.vi: Quyền riêng tư quan trọng với người lớn tuổi hay người trẻ hơn?

lines.t: Younger people share more, but research suggests they care about privacy just as much — they just manage it differently, for instance by using private accounts or messaging apps instead of public posts.
lines.vi: Người trẻ chia sẻ nhiều hơn, nhưng nghiên cứu cho thấy họ quan tâm đến quyền riêng tư không kém — chỉ là quản lý khác đi, chẳng hạn dùng tài khoản riêng tư hay ứng dụng nhắn tin thay vì đăng công khai.

sents.t: Governments sometimes argue that collecting metadata is harmless because it does not include the content of communications.
sents.vi: Các chính phủ đôi khi cho rằng thu thập siêu dữ liệu là vô hại vì nó không bao gồm nội dung liên lạc.

sents.t: However, a study at Stanford University showed that phone metadata alone could reveal sensitive information about people’s lives.
sents.vi: Tuy nhiên, một nghiên cứu ở Đại học Stanford cho thấy chỉ riêng siêu dữ liệu điện thoại có thể tiết lộ thông tin nhạy cảm về cuộc sống con người.

sents.t: From the times and numbers of calls, researchers could infer that participants had medical conditions or had visited certain clinics.
sents.vi: Từ thời điểm và số điện thoại của các cuộc gọi, các nhà nghiên cứu có thể suy ra người tham gia mắc bệnh hay đã đến một số phòng khám.

sents.t: The researchers emphasised that this required no special technology, only careful analysis.
sents.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu nhấn mạnh rằng điều này không cần công nghệ đặc biệt, chỉ cần phân tích cẩn thận.

sents.t: Their findings have been cited in legal challenges to mass data collection.
sents.vi: Kết quả của họ đã được dẫn chứng trong các vụ kiện phản đối việc thu thập dữ liệu hàng loạt.

q.q: Metadata includes the content of phone conversations.
The researchers did not need specialised technology.
The study led to a ban on metadata collection in the US.

gram.title: The formal subjunctive
gram.rule: recommend / insist / demand / propose / require + that + subject + base verb · It is essential / vital / imperative that + subject + base verb (be, have, not do)
gram.note: After verbs and adjectives of necessity or recommendation, formal English uses the base form of the verb for every subject, including he, she and it: The committee recommended that the law be reviewed. Negative: that he not be informed. British English often uses should instead (that the law should be reviewed), which is also correct.

ex.t: Campaigners demanded that the database be deleted.
ex.vi: Các nhà vận động đòi xoá bỏ cơ sở dữ liệu.

ex.t: It is essential that every request be approved by a judge.
ex.vi: Điều thiết yếu là mọi yêu cầu phải được thẩm phán phê duyệt.

ex.t: The report recommends that users be told how their data is used.
ex.vi: Báo cáo khuyến nghị người dùng phải được thông báo cách dữ liệu của họ được sử dụng.

ex.t: The law requires that companies not sell data without consent.
ex.vi: Luật yêu cầu công ty không được bán dữ liệu khi chưa có sự đồng ý.

drill.vi: Điều tối quan trọng là hệ thống phải an toàn.

drill.vi: Thẩm phán ra lệnh huỷ dữ liệu.

lines.t: Is it acceptable for governments to monitor citizens to prevent crime?
lines.vi: Chính phủ giám sát công dân để ngăn tội phạm có chấp nhận được không?

lines.t: Targeted monitoring, with a warrant and independent oversight, seems reasonable — that’s how police investigations have always worked. Mass surveillance of everyone is different. It treats the entire population as suspects, and history suggests that powers introduced for one purpose tend to expand to others.
lines.vi: Giám sát có mục tiêu, có lệnh và giám sát độc lập, có vẻ hợp lý — điều tra của cảnh sát vốn hoạt động như vậy. Giám sát hàng loạt mọi người thì khác. Nó coi toàn bộ dân chúng là nghi phạm, và lịch sử cho thấy quyền lực được tạo ra cho một mục đích thường mở rộng sang mục đích khác.

lines.t: What do you think of the argument “If you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear”?
lines.vi: Bạn nghĩ gì về lập luận “Không có gì để giấu thì không có gì phải sợ”?

lines.t: I think it misunderstands what privacy is for. Everyone has things that are legal but private — medical issues, financial problems, relationships. And what counts as “wrong” depends on who’s in power; information that’s harmless today could be used against people under a different government.
lines.vi: Tôi nghĩ nó hiểu sai mục đích của quyền riêng tư. Ai cũng có những điều hợp pháp nhưng riêng tư — sức khoẻ, tài chính, các mối quan hệ. Và điều gì bị coi là “sai” phụ thuộc vào ai đang nắm quyền; thông tin vô hại hôm nay có thể bị dùng chống lại người dân dưới một chính quyền khác.

lines.t: Are companies a bigger threat to privacy than governments?
lines.vi: Doanh nghiệp có phải mối đe doạ lớn hơn chính phủ đối với quyền riêng tư không?

lines.t: In everyday terms, possibly, because they collect far more detailed data and their business model depends on monetising it. But governments have powers companies don’t — they can arrest you. So the most worrying situation is when the two combine, with authorities able to access corporate data without proper safeguards.
lines.vi: Xét đời thường thì có thể, vì họ thu thập dữ liệu chi tiết hơn nhiều và mô hình kinh doanh dựa trên việc kiếm tiền từ nó. Nhưng chính phủ có quyền lực mà doanh nghiệp không có — họ có thể bắt giữ bạn. Nên tình huống đáng lo nhất là khi hai bên kết hợp, cơ quan chức năng có thể truy cập dữ liệu doanh nghiệp mà không có biện pháp bảo vệ phù hợp.

gram2.title: Inverted conditionals
gram2.rule: Should + subject + verb (= If … should) · Were + subject + to + verb (= If … were to) · Had + subject + past participle (= If … had)
gram2.note: In formal writing, you can omit if and invert the subject and auxiliary. Should you require assistance… is a polite formal condition. Were governments to ban encryption, … describes a hypothetical future. Had the data been encrypted, the breach would not have occurred refers to the past. These are rare and impressive — use one at most per essay.

ex.t: Should a breach occur, users must be informed immediately.
ex.vi: Nếu xảy ra rò rỉ, người dùng phải được thông báo ngay.

ex.t: Were encryption to be banned, criminals would simply use illegal tools.
ex.vi: Nếu mã hoá bị cấm, tội phạm sẽ đơn giản dùng công cụ bất hợp pháp.

ex.t: Had the company encrypted its files, the leak would have been harmless.
ex.vi: Nếu công ty mã hoá tệp, vụ rò rỉ đã vô hại.

ex.t: Should you have any questions, please contact us.
ex.vi: Nếu có câu hỏi, xin vui lòng liên hệ chúng tôi.

drill.t: ___ I known, I would have deleted it.
drill.vi: Nếu tôi biết, tôi đã xoá nó.

cue.card: Describe a time when you were concerned about your personal information being shared.
points: how it was shared or might have been shared
and explain how you felt about the situation
model: I’d like to talk about an incident about three years ago, when I received a phone call from someone claiming to be from my bank. The caller knew my full name, my address, the last four digits of my card and — this was the unsettling part — the name of the insurance product I had bought a few weeks earlier.

They said there had been suspicious activity on my account and asked me to confirm a code that had just been sent to my phone. Fortunately, something about the urgency of their tone made me hesitate, so I said I’d call the bank back myself. When I did, the bank confirmed it was a scam, and that the code would have allowed the caller to authorise a transfer. What I never found out was how they had obtained such specific details. The most likely explanation, the bank suggested, was a data breach at a third party — perhaps the insurance company or one of its agents.

I froze my card, changed all my passwords and filed a complaint, but I never received a clear explanation from either company, which was frustrating. I think what affected me most was the feeling of being exposed without having done anything careless. It made the abstract idea of a “data breach” very concrete. Since then I’ve been far more reluctant to give personal details to businesses, and I’m convinced that it is essential that companies be legally required to tell customers when their data has been compromised.

write.prompt: Many governments now use technology such as facial recognition cameras in public places to improve security. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
plan: Introduction: paraphrase + clear answer (disadvantages outweigh for mass deployment; targeted, regulated use acceptable)
Body 1: advantages — crime detection, missing persons, deterrence; fair, specific
Body 2: disadvantages — error rates and bias, chilling effect, function creep, data security; evidence
Conclusion: answer + conditions (legislation, warrants, independent oversight, transparency)
model: The use of facial recognition cameras in streets, stations and other public spaces has expanded rapidly as governments seek new ways to enhance security. Although this technology offers genuine benefits for law enforcement, I believe that, in its current form of widespread and loosely regulated deployment, its disadvantages outweigh its advantages.

Supporters of facial recognition point to several clear benefits. The technology can identify suspects far more quickly than human officers reviewing hours of footage, and it has helped police locate missing children and vulnerable adults within minutes rather than days. Its visible presence may also deter some crimes, such as theft and violence in crowded transport hubs. For citizens who feel unsafe in public spaces, these are not trivial gains, and it would be unrealistic to expect authorities to ignore a tool that can make investigations considerably more efficient.

However, these advantages come at a substantial cost. Independent testing has shown that some systems are markedly less accurate for women and people with darker skin, so errors are not randomly distributed but fall disproportionately on certain groups, potentially leading to wrongful stops or arrests. More fundamentally, constant identification in public spaces alters the relationship between citizens and the state. When people know that their every movement can be recorded, they may avoid lawful protests or sensitive locations, such as clinics or places of worship — a chilling effect that weakens civil liberties. There is also the risk of function creep: databases created to catch serious criminals may gradually be used for minor offences or political monitoring, and any centralised store of biometric data is an attractive target for hackers.

In conclusion, while facial recognition can make policing more effective, the risks of discrimination, the erosion of freedom and the misuse of data outweigh these benefits when the technology is deployed on a mass scale. Were it to be used at all, it is essential that its use be restricted to serious crimes, authorised by a judge in each case and subject to independent oversight and full public transparency.

units.title: Free speech & online platforms
units.goal: Discuss the limits of free expression and platform responsibility, using argumentative discourse markers and precise reporting.

words.ex: Freedom of expression is a fundamental right.

words.ex: Algorithms amplify outrage.
